Reported with the one-sided 95 % Clopper–Pearson upper bound on k of n (rule H), none after a futility stop.
  - What k can show (DERIVED, as REG-18), n = 5: k = 3 gives p ∈ [0.189, 0.924], k = 4 [0.343, 0.990], k = 5 [0.549, 1].
- **Futility stop:** REG-18's (`reg18_continue`): after each copied pair, `uv run python -m analysis.gate reg19_step` once, printing only the seeds done and `continue`; False once k + seeds left < 3, or on `surge_reading_wrong` or `controls_not_healthy`; a seed with no valid pair after its reruns stops the queue (`reg19_step` raises if a later seed has a run). After a stop: "k of n on seeds …, run in the order 15–19; stopped because ≥ 3 was out of reach", no bound.
- **Order** (`gate.reg19_order`), a rule fixed before the schedules were computed: exposed seeds first (REG-18 R2-T1, so the stop cannot skip a likely control failure), then the rest, ascending within each group. With no seed exposed: **15, 16, 17, 18, 19** (`test_reg19_inputs_schedule_facts`; the rule itself: `test_reg19_order_rule_puts_exposed_seeds_first`).
- **Readouts, never decisive:** k_c1 (C1's test alone); **k_18** (review T2): REG-18's per-seed rule (`reg18_seed_outcome`) applied to these runs: REG-17's per-span cold side on REG-8's three spans (600–1500 s after the burst's end) and the control's waiting in those spans. It differs from REG-18 in one respect only: both runs' verdicts and the cold side's end-window slope come from the 3000 s watch (judged at 4080 s), since the runs have no 1500 s verdict; so a control that goes cold after 2580 s changes `outcome_18` too (R2-N4); counts of each outcome; per seed W's c and λp, the eight spans' c, λp and `below`, `q_first` (mean waiting in W's first span), `q_end`, their ratio and the end-window slope (N3), the total line at W's start and end (N2: W's cold side holds exactly when the line grows by more than (λp_W − c)·2400 requests, DERIVED from completions = planned − Δline), `drain_time` and the after-empty readouts, `end_window` including unreleased turns (N7), both runs' `surge_run`, the control's waiting per span (read over W only, as REG-18 read REG-8's spans; not over the first 600 s after the burst, N6), REG-8's span label, release rate, shock size, turn-0 share; **burst run against control before the burst** (review T3, `gate.reg19_baseline_pair`): over [300, 900) s, pf, hit, median TTFT, SM clock and power over busy samples, temperature, completion rate (set by the identical arrivals, so it carries little signal), and their differences; **`order_flag`** (R2-N3, fixed now): the burst run's pf lower than the control's by more than `recovered_pf_drop` 0.02, or its busy SM clock lower by more than `max_sm_clock_cv` 0.05 (relative). A flagged pass is reported as open to the run-order alternative; REG-17's seed 2 and REG-18's seeds beside the table, not counted, not pooled.
- **Prediction** (BELIEF), per seed: burst-run baseline pf ≥ 0.98 ≈ 0.85 (4 of 5 at 2.0 so far; REG-18's seed 5 at 0.978); control `recovered` through 4080 s ≈ 0.9 (5 of 5 at 2.0 so far; no seed exposed); burst `stuck` at 3000 s without the line emptying ≈ 0.75 (seed 18 ≈ 0.5, its 1.32 first span); W's cold side given that ≈ 0.95 (W's λp 1.92–2.08 against cold rates 1.67–1.80 so far). So P(pass) ≈ 0.55 per seed, seed 18 ≈ 0.36. Then (DERIVED, independent seeds, exact enumeration) E[k] ≈ 2.5, P(k = 0) ≈ 0.03, P(k = 1–2) ≈ 0.46, **P(k ≥ 3) ≈ 0.52**. k_clear ≈ k (no control has queued at 2.0 so far). Under the futility stop: 3 seeds run with P ≈ 0.09, 4 ≈ 0.22, all 5 ≈ 0.69; 4.6 expected. Readouts if stuck: W's c ≈ 1.70–1.82; `q_end` 60–250; **k_18 likely 0–2** (every seed has a span below 1.84), so a `supports` will almost certainly rest on the new test (review T2). Matrix stops (N4, DERIVED from the 0.9 per control): P(2 or more bad controls) ≈ 0.08; P(any control not `recovered`) ≈ 0.41; with no seed exposed, any control that tips is `control_cold_no_surge`, so if about half of control failures are tips (BELIEF), P(`surge_reading_wrong`) ≈ 0.23.
- **Decision under each outcome:**
  - **Wording fixed now for any pass result (review T2):** "At λ = 2.0, after the burst the server stayed stuck, cold and below its load through a 3000 s watch without the line emptying, while the same schedule without the burst stayed healthy, in k of n new seeds (15–19), under REG-19's whole-window test, written after REG-18's matrix (1 of 4 under the per-span test). Under REG-18's per-span test on the same runs: k_18 of n." If k_18 < 3, the report says that the result rests on the new test.
  - **`supports` (k_clear ≥ 3):** draft C1's confirmation at λ = 2.0 for the owner: a 4500 s watch, then a drop to λ = 1 long enough for the line to empty (REG-16's calibration), then the return (conditions 5–6), on a seed chosen by a rule fixed before its schedule is read. Report the cell as "stuck in k of n" with the bound, under REG-19's test (named as a new test, written after REG-18). C1's status changes only after the owner reviews it.
  - **`supports_edge`:** reported as such; the owner decides whether the confirmation is drafted.
  - **`some` or `none` (or a stop), read by what failed:** if `drains` (the burst run's verdict at 4080 s is `recovered` or `slow_drain`) is 2 or more of the seeds run (`n_drains`; R2-T1: no `emptied_*` label counts here), the λ = 2.0 cold states are long drains, not stuck: the agent drafts the report of the zone as too narrow for this workload at L1, for the owner. Otherwise (failures mostly `emptied_retipped`, `emptied_cold`, `emptied_unclear`, `stuck_not_cold`, `bad_baseline`, `inconclusive` or `unclear`), the owner chooses, with no recommendation drafted beforehand, between λ = 2.1 and the report.
  - **`controls_not_healthy`:** λ = 2.0 is not reliably warm over 4080 s with these schedules; the owner decides.
  - **`surge_reading_wrong`:** stop; rethink before anything else is drafted.
  - **The queue stops for an operational reason:** no table; runs reported from `checks.json` only; the owner decides.
- **Alternatives to read against each outcome:**
  1. **`supports` from overload, not metastability:** the controls run the identical schedule for 4080 s; their waiting share per span and end hit separate a load the warm state carries from one it does not. W's λp is 1.92–2.08, at λ.
  2. **A test fitted to REG-18:** new seeds protect against fitting noise, not against choosing a test that is lax exactly where the last one failed. Separated by `k_18` beside k: if k_18 ≈ k, the change did not matter; if k_18 ≪ k, the result rests on the new test, and the wording above says so.
  3. **Stuck at 3000 s but draining later:** 3000 s does not show a permanent state; only the confirmation with its drop separates it. A `q_ratio` well below 1 with a negative end slope (but not within `drain_horizon_s`) points to a long drain.
  4. **A closed-loop ceiling, not a stuck server:** in the closed loop a session's next turn waits for the previous one, so the queue is bounded and can sit flat; a flat high queue at hit 0, KV 0.95 is still the cold state. `unreleased` turns and `release_rate` against c show whether the clients, not the server, set the level.
  5. **Run order (review T3):** in every pair the control runs first and the burst run about 70 min later, on a warmer card. A burst run a few percent slower before its burst has a thinner margin at λ = 2.0 and could stick for that reason alone (REG-18's burst-run baselines were pf 0.978–0.995). Separated by `reg19_baseline_pair`: completion rate, pf, SM clock and power before the burst, burst run minus control. The owner may instead alternate the order by seed parity (a design change, offered at approval).
  6. **Instrument gaps:** a burst-run baseline at 0.978–0.987 (REG-18) sits near `min_baseline_pf` 0.98; a `bad_baseline` counts against and is not rerun. **Heat over ≈ 11 h:** `gpu_steady`, `power_limit` per run in run order. **Limits:** single control per seed (rule H); closed loop, L1, 350 W only.
- **Stopping rule:** REG-18's. Each run once; an invalid run (other than `burst_min_kv_max`) is rerun unchanged, at most twice; no rerun on any verdict or label; a heat-invalid run once after cooling to ≤ 45 °C, a second heat failure stops the queue; a `client_error`, a burst that does not fill the pool (`burst_min_kv_max`), a limit other than 350 W, or an unexpected pre-launch check stops the queue. A rerun decision reads only `checks.json`. No interim look beyond `reg19_step`'s `continue` flag.
- **Order of work:** seeds 15, 16, 17, 18, 19; in each the control first, then the burst run, each after the pre-launch checks (350 W, ≤ 45 °C, idle GPU, clean tree at the registered commit, disk); reads in `docs/probe/<date>_reg19/`. Each pair copied to the Mac and checksum-verified before `reg19_step`.
- **Result, computed once after the queue ends:** `uv run python -m analysis.gate reg19` (`gate.reg19_table`).
- **Cost** (DERIVED; review N5): 4080 s of arrivals + 108 s start-up per run (REG-17's 2688 − 2580) gives 2.33 h per seed; REG-18's seeds took 96 min each from control launch to control launch against 86 min of arrivals (11:09 → 12:45 → 14:21 UTC, [OPS] 2026-11-11), so with copy, checks and the burst run's drain ≈ 2.45 h. **≈ 10.7–11.3 h expected** under the futility stop (4.6 seeds), 11.6–12.3 h for all five; worst case with every run rerun twice ≈ 35–37 h plus cooling. Disk ≈ 240 MB per run (REG-18's ≈ 150 MB × 4080 / 2580), ≈ 2.4 GB for ten; the VM has 7.3 GB free.
- **Code and files:** `analysis/gate.py` (`REG19`, `PASS19`, `EMPTIED19`, `reg19_spec`, `reg19_exposed`, `reg19_order`, `reg19_spans`, `reg19_cold_side`, `reg19_emptyings`, `reg19_drain_time`, `reg19_after_empty`, `reg19_baseline_pair`, `reg19_seed_outcome`, `reg19_pair`, `reg19_outcome`, `reg19_step`, `reg19_table`, `reg19_inputs`; `python -m analysis.gate reg19 | reg19_inputs | reg19_step`); the 10 configs; `tests/test_gate.py` (13 new: configs change only seed, watch and duration; the seeds are new; schedule facts and the order; the order rule; the patterns never pick a 1500 s run or another seed; the per-seed rules, including the three `emptied_*` labels before a NaN cold side and the control first; `reg19_drain_time` needs 30 s of zeros inside the arrivals (N1); `reg19_emptyings` lists every emptying (R2-N2); `reg19_after_empty` reads re-warming, a late re-warm, the re-tip time, a cold empty line, NaN, and stops at 4080 s (T1, R2-T1, R2-T2, R2-N1); the matrix counts the new labels against; `reg19_step` never skips a seed; a missing run is refused; the cold side on a synthetic run, including a quiet span that fails alone).
- **Not changed:** harness, checks, thresholds (`min_baseline_pf`, `max_control_waiting`, `surge_tip`, the verdict's), PROTOCOL, REG-17's and REG-18's functions and results.

### Adversarial review (separate subagent; it saw only the first draft, its diff, and the code and configs those call; it opened no runs and no docs). Round 1, verbatim:

> ## Rule F review: REG-19 draft
>
> **Reproduced.** `uv run pytest -q tests/test_gate.py -k reg19` passes 10 of 10. `gate.reg19_inputs()` gives back the draft's table digit for digit: request counts, λp for baseline, W and each span, lowest span, the control peaks 3.092, 2.875, 3.017, 2.908 and 2.833 at the stated times, no seed exposed, each control schedule equal to its burst run's session rows, watch (3000, 3000), duration (4080, 4080), and order (15, 16, 17, 18, 19). The prediction checks out by exact enumeration with p = 0.55 per seed and 0.36 for seed 18: E[k] = 2.56, P(k=0) = 0.026, P(k=1–2) = 0.45, P(k≥3) = 0.523. Under the futility stop the queue ends after 3 seeds with probability 0.091, after 4 with 0.214, and runs all 5 with 0.695, for 4.60 expected seeds. The unrounded factors (0.85·0.9·0.75·0.95 = 0.545) give 0.517 and 4.60. Cost: 2 × (4080 + 108) s = 2.33 h per seed, 11.63 h for five, 10.70 h expected, 34.9 h worst case. Disk: 150 × 4080 / 2580 = 237 MB per run. No mismatches. I tested `reg19_seed_outcome` on synthetic inputs and every branch returns what the draft says, including `stuck_emptied` when the cold side is NaN and `inconclusive` for an empty or NaN control share.
>
> ### Should-fix
>
> - **T1. `stuck_emptied` measures the server queue, but the decision reads it as a drain.** `drain_time` looks only at `vllm:num_requests_waiting`. `owed_backlog` (its docstring calls it "the total line") also counts closed-loop turns not yet released. Trace: on seed 18, the first span of W plans 1.32 req/s. A cold server completing about 1.75 req/s empties its waiting queue for 30 s or more while the hit rate stays near 0 and the clients still hold turns. Load comes back, the queue rebuilds, and the run ends `stuck` with the cold side holding. The label is `stuck_emptied`, and the decision rule ("`stuck_emptied` + `drains` ≥ 2 ⇒ long drains, not stuck ⇒ report the zone as too narrow") then draws the wrong conclusion. **Fix:** register readouts at `drain_time`: the hit rate and KV usage over the next 60–120 s, and `owed_backlog` there against its baseline level. Then split the label into `emptied_rewarmed` (hit back within `recovered_hit_drop` of baseline) and `emptied_cold`. Only `emptied_rewarmed` should feed the "long drains" branch; `emptied_cold` should go to the owner.
>
> - **T2. The comparison meant to guard against forking paths is not REG-18's rule.** `c_17` is `c1` (from the 4080 s verdict) combined with `reg17_cold_side.holds`. That cold side uses the slope of the 3480–4080 s end window. It ignores the control's waiting and the clear/edge split. So "what REG-18's rule would have said" is a hybrid of the two rules. The draft's main defence of a test written after seeing the data is "k_17 ≈ k vs k_17 ≪ k". **Fix:** compute `k_18 = Σ[reg18_seed_outcome(…, reg17_cold_side(burst)["holds"], …) ∈ PASS18]` on these runs, and describe it exactly. Also state now that the draft itself predicts k_17 = 0–2, so `supports` will almost certainly rest on the new test. The claim's wording for that case should be fixed in the entry now, not left to the report.
>
> - **T3. Run order is confounded with the treatment, and no alternative names it.** In every pair the control runs first and the burst run about 1.2 h later. The draft itself notes that REG-18's burst-run baselines sit at 0.978–0.987, close to `min_baseline_pf`. A burst run that is a few percent slower before its burst has a thinner margin at λ = 2.0, and that alone could make it stick. **Fix:** add this as alternative 6. Register a readout per pair comparing burst and control over the baseline [300, 900): completion rate, pf, SM clock and power. Offer the owner the option of alternating the order by seed parity; that is a design change, so it is the owner's call.
>
> ### Minor
>
> - **N1.** `drain_time` drops scrapes from 4080 s on. A zero at t ≥ 4050 s therefore counts as "emptied" on fewer than 30 s of data. Fix: require t_i + 30 ≤ 4080.
> - **N2.** The whole-window cold side is equivalent to the owed backlog growing over W (DERIVED: completions in W = planned in W − Δowed). Where λp_W > 2.0 it requires growth of more than (λp_W − 2.0) × 2400 requests: 185, 91, 98 and 125 for seeds 15, 16, 17 and 19. That is not trivial, and with cold rates of 1.67–1.80 it is not impossible either. Report `owed_backlog` at 1680 s and at 4080 s so readers can see the equivalence. Burst completions in W raise c, which works against a pass; that is conservative.
> - **N3.** A queue can pass while draining. Example: it rises to about 200 by 3880 s, then falls with slope −0.04/s. That is still net growth over W, with q/−slope = 3750 s > 3600 s, so the verdict is `stuck` and the run passes. Alternative 3 covers this case. Add `q_ratio` and the end slope to the table.
> - **N4.** The prediction leaves out the outcomes that stop the matrix. A control that goes cold over 4080 s with a peak below 3.2 gives `surge_reading_wrong`, and two bad controls stop the queue. Give P(≥ 2 bad controls) and P(any `control_cold_no_surge`) from the stated 0.9.
> - **N5.** The cost leaves out cooling to ≤ 45 °C between runs, the copy and checksum, and drain time beyond 108 s for a backlogged burst run (up to `drain_s` 300). Give the cost as a range.
> - **N6.** The control's waiting is not read over [1080, 1680). That matches REG-18, but say so.
> - **N7.** In the end window, turns that are never released are scored as misses and lower the burst run's pf. The hit-rate condition of `stuck` is not affected. Report `end_window.unreleased`.
>
> ### Alternative explanations
>
> - **For `supports`:**
>   - **Run order and heat (T3).** Separated by the baseline comparison between burst and control.
>   - **Sustained overload, not hysteresis.** At λ = 2.0 the cold rate is below λ by construction, so 3000 s cannot tell "stuck" from "a very long drain". Only the confirmation drop separates them, as the draft says.
> - **For `some` / `none`:**
>   - **Quiet spans in the schedule.** Seed 18's 1.32 span, or any span below about 1.8, lets the waiting queue empty while the server stays cold (T1). This is the schedule, not the server.
>   - **Instrument limits.** A burst-run baseline pf near 0.98 makes `bad_baseline` likely. Heat over runs of about 70 min can invalidate them.
>
> ### Can the run change a decision?
>
> Yes. `supports` leads to drafting the confirmation; the failure branches lead to the zone report or to λ = 2.1. The test is defensible only because it is judged on fresh seeds. Fresh seeds protect against fitting noise, but not against choosing a test that is lax exactly where the last one failed. That is why T2's clean counterfactual and the claim's wording fixed in advance are needed.
>
> ### Verdict
>
> **Not ready for the owner's approval yet.** The arithmetic, schedule facts, code paths and safeguards (seed and watch checks, no skipping, NaN handling, the stop) are correct. Before registration:
> 1. Split `stuck_emptied` by whether the server re-warmed, and send only the re-warmed case to "long drains" (T1).
> 2. Replace `k_17` with a true REG-18 counterfactual, and fix the claim's wording for the case where only the new test passes (T2).
> 3. Name the run-order confound and add its baseline readout (T3).
>
> After those three changes it can go to the owner. The minor items can be folded in at the same time.

- **Changed because of it:**
  - T1: the line emptying is split by what the server did then (`reg19_after_empty`: hit over the next 120 s against the baseline, KV, the total line): `emptied_rewarmed`, `emptied_cold`, `emptied_unclear`; none is a pass, and only `emptied_rewarmed` (with `drains`) feeds the "long drains" branch. Tested.
  - T2: `k_17` is replaced by `k_18`, REG-18's own per-seed rule (`reg18_seed_outcome`) on these runs, described exactly (it differs only in using the 3000 s watch's verdicts and end slope). The prediction now states k_18 is likely 0–2, and the wording of any pass result is fixed in the entry, naming the new test and k_18.
  - T3: run order is alternative 5; `reg19_baseline_pair` reports burst run against control before the burst (completion rate, pf, hit, SM clock, power, temperature). Alternating the order by seed parity is offered to the owner at approval. Checked to run on an existing pair (values not read).
  - N1: `reg19_drain_time` needs its 30 s of zeros to end by 4080 s (REG-17's `drain_time` unchanged). Tested. N2, N3, N7: the total line at W's start and end, `q_ratio`, the end slope and unreleased turns are in the table. N4: the matrix-stop probabilities are in the prediction. N5: the cost is a range, from REG-18's measured 96 min per seed. N6: stated.

### Round 2 (separate subagent; it saw only the revised draft with round 1 and its changes, the full diff, and the code and configs those call; no runs, no docs). Verbatim:

> ## Rule F review, round 2: REG-19
>
> **Reproduced.** `pytest -k reg19`: 12 of 12 pass. `reg19_inputs` matches the table again, and the order is 15–19. The N4 numbers check out: P(≥2 bad controls) = 1 − 0.9⁵ − 5·0.1·0.9⁴ = 0.082, P(any) = 0.41, P(surge_reading_wrong) = 1 − 0.95⁵ = 0.23. The cost checks out: 4.6 × 2.33–2.45 h = 10.7–11.3 h. I traced `reg19_seed_outcome` again, including the `drained` with a NaN cold side case and the `stuck_draining` → `emptied_*` / `stuck_not_cold` mapping, and every branch matches the text. `outcome_18` uses REG-8's spans, `reg17_cold_side` at λ 2.0, the control's waiting over those same spans, and an exposure that is false to both 2580 s and 4080 s, so it is REG-18's rule except for the stated verdict time. `reg19_baseline_pair` uses the real GPU columns (`util_pct`, `sm_clock_mhz`, `power_w`, `temp_c`, recorder.py) on the same t0 as the metrics, and `gpu_busy_util_pct` exists (base.yaml:58).
>
> ### Should-fix
>
> - **R2-T1. `emptied_rewarmed` together with a `stuck` verdict means the server re-tipped. It is not a long drain.** That label applies only when the burst verdict at 4080 s is `stuck`, so the end hit is ≤ baseline − `stuck_hit_drop`. The sequence is: the line empties, the hit comes back within 0.06 of baseline, and then the server goes cold again, while the control on the same schedule never does. That is a second tip after recovery. It is either fragility near the edge or a carry-over from the burst. It is not "the λ = 2.0 cold states are long drains". Feeding it into the `n_emptied_rewarmed_or_drains` branch puts the wrong reason into the zone report. **Fix:** rename it (for example `emptied_retipped`). Add a readout of when the cold state came back (KV onset or hit drop after `drain_time`). Fix its branch now: I suggest the owner chooses, and only `drains` feeds "long drains".
> - **R2-T2. The after-empty window runs past the end of the recording.** N1 allows an emptying up to 4050 s, but `reg19_after_empty` reads [t, t + 120 s), which can reach 4170 s. Once the line has emptied, the loadgen finishes within seconds of 4080 s and the recorder stops (run.py:192–202), so `_covered` fails. Trace: synthetic run, waiting 0 from 4000 s, hit 0.8 against a baseline of 0.8, scrapes end at 4085 s. Result: `drain_time` = 2920 s, `rewarmed` = None, label `emptied_unclear`. A real late drain becomes "unclear" and drops out of the drains count. **Fix:** read [t, min(t + 120, duration)). Say what happens when fewer than 60 s remain: either `unclear`, or require t ≤ duration − 120 before an emptying counts as drained. Register the choice now.
>
> ### Minor
>
> - **R2-N1.** No source supports the 120 s re-warm window. Right after the line empties, each session's next turn has to re-prefill its prefix, so the hit stays below baseline for a while even on a server that is truly recovering. That pushes results toward `emptied_cold`. Cite a recovery time from an existing run (for example the REG-16 drop phase) or use a later window, and fix the choice before the run (rule 7).
> - **R2-N2.** `reg19_drain_time` uses only the first emptying. If the line first empties cold in seed 18's 1.32 span and later empties re-warmed, the seed is labelled `emptied_cold`. Report every emptying (time and hit) as a readout. The label can stay on the first.
> - **R2-N3.** No interpretation rule is registered for the T3 readout. Before the run, state which burst-minus-control difference will be read as a run-order confound. For example: pf lower by more than `recovered_pf_drop`, or SM clock lower by more than `gpu_steady`'s CV tolerance. The completion rate over [300, 900) is set by the identical arrivals, so its difference carries almost no signal. Rely on pf, TTFT, clock and power instead.
> - **R2-N4.** "k_18 differs in one respect only" is accurate for the counterfactual. Also say that the control's verdict comes from 4080 s, not 2580 s, so a control that goes cold after 2580 s changes `outcome_18`.
>
> The original N1–N7 items are handled as claimed: N1 is coded and tested; `owed`, `q_ratio`, `end_q_slope` and `unreleased_end` are in the table rows; N4 and N5 are in the text; N6 is stated.
>
> ### Verdict
>
> **Not ready yet, but close.** T2 and T3 are fixed correctly. T1's split is in place, but it hands the "long drains" branch the wrong case (R2-T1), and its 120 s window reads NaN for any emptying in the last two minutes (R2-T2). Both fixes are small and touch only `reg19_after_empty` and the label and branch text. Once they are made and tested, along with the registered choices in R2-N1 and R2-N3, the entry can go to the owner without another review round.

- **Changed because of it:**
  - R2-T1: the re-warmed case is now `emptied_retipped` (warm again, then cold by 4080 s); `t_recold` reads when it went cold again. Only `drains` feeds the "long drains" branch (`n_drains`); every `emptied_*` label goes to the owner. Tested.
  - R2-T2: the after-empty windows are cut at the end of arrivals and read only if at least 60 s long; an emptying with less than 60 s left is `emptied_unclear` (registered now). Tested on the review's trace (emptying at 4030 s: no window read) and at 3980 s (one 100 s window).
  - R2-N1: the hit is read in 120 s windows starting every 60 s up to 600 s (2τ) after the emptying; a re-warm after the first 120 s counts. 600 s is chosen now with no run behind it; stated as such. Tested.
  - R2-N2: `reg19_emptyings` lists every emptying; the label uses the first. Tested. R2-N3: `order_flag` registered (pf lower by > 0.02, or busy SM clock lower by > 5 %), median TTFT added; the completion rate noted as low-signal. R2-N4: stated.
- **Not covered:** no third review round (the round-2 reviewer said none was needed after these fixes); the round-2 fixes were checked by tests only. The new readouts were run once on an existing REG-18 pair to check they execute (values not read). The run waits for the owner's approval of this registration.

## 2026-11-12 · [DECISION] Owner adopts Paper Plan v3: existence becomes a cited premise, the paper's claims move to the boundary (K1–K5); C6, C8 and C9 dropped; a session-cap arm replaces the protected-prefixes control; the paper's C1 metric is hit rate and SLO share
- **Why now:** three preprints dated 2–10 November 2026 report the failure this study set out to show: Lu et al., arXiv 2611.02543; Valse and Jannesari, arXiv 2611.08902 (tests on SGLang and on vLLM 0.32.0, the version pinned here); Huang and Liu, arXiv 2611.13412. Each reports a burst that leaves a prefix-cached engine cold and backlogged at a load its no-burst twin sustains, with no client retries; Huang and Liu and Lu et al. also publish an admission controller of the kind planned as C9. Everything said here about these papers is BELIEF: the agent read them through automated summaries (no figures; Lu et al. §5–10 not verbatim), and none of it has been checked against the papers (open-questions A16).
- **Owner (2026-11-12):** asked for a comparison with the three preprints and a recommendation; chose to refine the thesis, not replace it ("ok, draft Paper Plan v3"); then "yes to all three, now update the repo docs", in reply to the three choices the draft made:
  1. **C6, C8 and C9 are dropped** from the paper (mitigation transfer, retries and residency, the admission controller). The published controllers are cited, not compared against.
  2. **A session-cap arm replaces the protected-prefixes control** as the control that cuts the loop (C2's test). The arm limits the number of sessions in service at the load generator; it has no config, code or registration yet, and running it is a workload change that needs its own `[REG]`. S4 (open-questions) is closed as dropped.
  3. **The paper states C1 in hit rate and SLO share (percent fast), not completions per second.** This agrees with the 2026-11-05 decision that the registered pf/hit/queue verdict judges every cell and the completion rate is a secondary readout. Reason: the stuck state here completes only 10–14 % less than the offered load (DERIVED: 1 − 1.77 / 2.0 = 0.115 and 1 − 1.73 / 2.0 = 0.135, from the span rates 1.73–1.77 req/s of decisions.md 2026-11-10 [RESULT] REG-17).
- **New claim structure** (full text with tests in `docs/claims.md`; the paper layer is `docs/paper/paper-plan-v3.md`, kept on the Mac and ignored by git through `.git/info/exclude`):
  - **P0, the premise:** C1 and C2, cited and replicated at this scale; no novelty is claimed for them. Their tests are unchanged.
  - **K1:** turn semantics decide the outcome (open-loop turns shield the cache, closed turns expose it).
  - **K2:** the vulnerable load range widens with per-session context and is empty when the reuse comes from one shared system prompt.
  - **K3:** the published models predict this setup's boundary within a tolerance fixed beforehand, or they do not.
  - **K4:** near the warm capacity the healthy state ends at an arrival surge.
  - **K5 (optional):** lead time of cache signals over latency.
- **Evidence in the repo that bears on the choice** (none of it new): with open-loop turns no shock run got stuck, 0 of 3 in each of 10 cells (FILE(PROTOCOL.md:105)); at L1, λ = 2.4, the open-loop burst run drained and the closed-loop one stuck, one seed each (decisions.md 2026-11-09 [RESULT] REG-10 and REG-11); at λ = 2.0 the registered matrix gave 1 of 4 (decisions.md 2026-11-11 [RESULT] REG-18). The system prompt is drawn per session, so no run so far has a shared prompt (FILE(harness/workload.py:97)).
- **Alternatives considered:** (a) keep the existence thesis: rejected, it is published three times and this study's registered test stands at 1 of 4; (b) replace the thesis with retries or detection only: rejected, it discards the open-loop runs and the closed-loop cells; (c) refine to the boundary: chosen. The agent's argument for (c) that is not evidence (BELIEF): its claims keep their value whether REG-19 passes or not.
- **What does not change:** REG-19 runs and is judged exactly as registered and approved (decisions.md 2026-11-11 [REG], [DECISION]); it had started before this entry (seed 15's pair is on the Mac, seed 16 was under way), and the agent writing this entry has read none of its results. No verdict code, threshold, check, config, workload or seed is changed by this entry. `PROTOCOL.md` §3–§6 are unchanged. `docs/experiment-plan.md` is not yet revised; that is the next step and each run in it needs its own `[REG]`.
- **Found while reading, not fixed here** (left to the session running REG-19, to avoid two sessions editing the same lines): `docs/status.md` gives three different run counts on the Mac (176 folders, "all 138", "all 125") and says "any run outside REG-8 needs 420 W" although REG-9 to REG-19 run at 350 W; its run list has no REG-18 or REG-19 runs, and `tools/check_docs.py` fails `inventory` (176 against 178 folders) for that reason; `PROTOCOL.md` §4 and §7 still describe only the open-loop setups and the 0-of-30 result.

## 2026-11-12 · [CORR] Paper Plan v3 and today's decision entry: a shared prompt was tested inside a mixed workload (Huang and Liu); the others' load range is 1.35–4.0, not 1.35–2.7; "10–14 %" misstated its own derivation; K2 gets definitions
- **Source of the corrections:** a review of `docs/paper/paper-plan-v3.md` passed on by the owner on 2026-11-12, then two targeted re-reads of the papers through fetch agents returning verbatim quotes. The agent's errors, all in text it wrote today:
  1. **"No preprint tests a shared prompt" was false.** Huang and Liu's synthetic sessions start with "a 2K-token system prompt shared by all sessions" (their §3), and their stuck state held in 9 of 12 pairs. The agent's own first summary of that paper already said so; the plan and two chat replies overstated the gap. Correct statement: no preprint varies or isolates the shared prompt. Their workload is mixed (2K shared inside a 6K–37K context; warm hit ratio 0.94–0.95), and they report the collapsed hit ratio of 0.10–0.12 as the shared prompt alone (their §4). **K2 now defines** cache gain, shared-only and matched cache gain (`docs/claims.md`, K2), so that a mixed workload is not read as a test of the shared-only prediction. Whether the definitions are the right ones is the owner's to confirm; they change a paper claim's wording, not its content.
  2. **"Loads 1.35 to 2.7 times the cold capacity" was wrong at the top and incomplete at the bottom.** Valse and Jannesari's registered burst rates are 1.35, 1.5, 1.65, 2.0, 2.5 and 4.0 λ_ref (their Table 1); Huang and Liu's loads are 2.7–3.1 times their drain break-even (DERIVED: 0.035 / 0.013 and 0.04 / 0.013). No burst test starts below 1.35. But two results sit near this study's margin of 1.19 and were left out: CUT-A held an already trapped engine at a realized 1.12–1.20 λ_ref after entry at 1.65, and a window of (1, 1.3) λ_ref on the H200 at a 300k pool was reported as too narrow to place a test (their §2; their H200 tests ran at a 600k pool, at 1.5 and 2.0). So the plan's "a regime their tests do not reach" is narrowed to: **entry by a burst** inside a narrow window (load 1.19, warm capacity 2.4 / 1.681 = 1.43 times the floor, DERIVED from `docs/model.md` M2, REG-8 and REG-13 rows). Persistence at such a margin is theirs.
  3. **"10–14 %" in today's [DECISION] (choice 3) does not match the derivation printed beside it,** which gives 11.5 % and 13.5 % (1 − 1.77 / 2.0 and 1 − 1.73 / 2.0). The derivation is right; the range should read "11.5–13.5 %". The same loose range was in the plan and in chat. (The review computed 9–13 % from 1.03–1.08 times the floor; the 1.08 comes from REG-14's 1.81 req/s, measured at λ = 2.2, so it does not apply at 2.0.) The owner's choice it supported is unaffected: completions/s still separates the states poorly.
  4. **"C1's metric" in the plan** used a label the plan itself retires; now "P0's metric". In the repo C1 stays the name of the test.
- **Changed:** `docs/paper/paper-plan-v3.md` (P0, K2, the adopt list, two prior-work rows); `docs/claims.md` (K2 claim wording, definitions, the prior result); `docs/open-questions.md` (A16: two items checked). Today's [DECISION] entry is left as written.

## 2026-11-12 · [DECISION] Design choices for the revised Stage 2: conditions 5–6 kept; session cap from the control's peak; shared-only workload of 2576 + 496 tokens; K2's second point is 16 turns, not a longer system prompt; closed-loop cold floor to be measured
- **Owner (2026-11-12):** "do whatever leads to correct results", in reply to the five open questions at the end of the revised Stage 2 section. The choices below are the agent's, made under that delegation; each enters a `[REG]` before any run, where the owner can change it. No run, config, code, check or threshold is changed here.
- **1. Conditions 5 and 6 of PROTOCOL §3 stay required for P0.** Persistence in the preprints is BELIEF about other setups. Condition 6 is the test that separates two states at one load from overload, and it has not been passed after a burst: REG-15's drop was `drop_inconclusive`, and REG-16 showed the return only in a no-burst run (decisions.md 2026-11-10 [RESULT] REG-15, REG-16). The drop's length is fixed beforehand from the expected backlog and the cold floor with a factor of two; 1800 s was too short and 9000 s enough in those two runs. Alternative rejected: dropping 5–6 because others showed them (it would make P0 a citation, not a replication).
- **2. Session cap value:** per seed, the highest number of sessions in service at once in the same seed's no-trigger control, a session being in service from its first turn sent to its last reply. Reasons: it is fixed by data that exist before the capped run; it needs no calibration runs; on the control's own schedule it never binds, so the capped arm differs from the burst run only when the population exceeds what the healthy run needed. Burst requests are one-off and pass the cap, so the trigger is the same in both arms. The capped arm is judged on the server's hit rate and waiting line; waiting at the cap is reported apart. Alternative rejected: the smallest population reaching 0.95 of the peak closed-population throughput (Valse and Jannesari's rule, BELIEF), which needs a calibration sweep per setup.
- **3. Shared-only workload:** L1's sessions unchanged in timing (8 turns, closed-loop, 5 s gaps, 128 output tokens), every turn one 2576-token prefix shared by all sessions plus 496 fresh tokens. DERIVED from L1's schedule (2048 system + 128 user tokens on turn 0, + 256 per later turn; FILE(configs/l1_base.yaml:9), FILE(PROTOCOL.md:54)): prompts 2176 … 3968, mean 3072; a warm later turn reuses the previous prompt, so cached tokens per session are 7 × 2176 + 256 × 21 = 20,608 of 24,576, hit 0.8385, uncached mean 496. The measured warm hit is 0.838 (decisions.md 2026-11-10 [RESULT] REG-17), which the calculation reproduces. 2576 = 161 blocks of 16, and 2576 / 3072 = 0.8385. Matched: mean prompt, mean uncached tokens, hit rate, session timing. Not matched: the spread of uncached tokens (2176 on a first turn, 256 after, against 496 on every turn); and the running batch holds far less memory, since the shared blocks are counted once, which is the property K2 is about.
- **4. K2's second point is the number of turns (16, then 4), not `system_tokens`.** With the system prompt drawn per session (FILE(harness/workload.py:97)), the ratio of cold to warm prefill tokens per turn is 8 (s + 1024) / (s + 1920) for a system prompt of s tokens (DERIVED): 5.05 at 512, 6.19 at 2048, 6.56 at 3072, so the lever is weak; and a first turn of s + 128 tokens is always uncached, which at the cold prefill rate implied by the floor (1.681 × 3072 ≈ 5160 tokens/s, DERIVED, BELIEF as a rate) takes about 0.6 s at s = 3072 and 0.8 s at 4096 against the 1.0 s limit, so longer prompts risk `bad_baseline`. With T turns at s = 2048 the ratio is 3.48 (T = 4), 6.19 (8), 10.9 (16) (DERIVED: T (2176 + 128 (T − 1)) / (2176 + 256 (T − 1))), and the first turn does not change. These token ratios are not the width of the load window, which also depends on decode time and the TTFT limit (the measured window at L1 is 2.4 / 1.681 = 1.43 closed-loop); they rank the levers and predict nothing by themselves. 16 turns is taken first because a wider gap should also give a stuck cell that holds in more seeds than L1's 1 of 4, which the K1 arm and the loop-cut controls need (BELIEF). Whether 16-turn sessions fit the pool warm is checked by that setup's own sweeps.
- **5. The cold floor for closed-loop cells is measured, not assumed.** 1.681 req/s is a cache-off saturation with open-loop turns on seed 0 (decisions.md 2026-11-07 [RESULT] REG-8), and the closed-loop cold states completed 1.73–1.81 req/s (`docs/model.md` M2, REG-14 and REG-17 rows). Two explanations: a cold closed-loop server serves more early, short turns (the published model's reading), or the floor differs with turn semantics. Step B compares uncached prefill tokens per second in the two conditions (0 GPU h), which separates them; every new setup's cache-off sweep uses closed-loop turns; for L1 a closed-loop cache-off sweep is registered before step C if step B's comparison is outside its tolerance. Until then the docs say "the open-loop floor".
- **Changed:** the answered list at the end of `docs/experiment-plan.md`, its step E and boundary map; K2's test in `docs/claims.md` and in `docs/paper/paper-plan-v3.md`.

## 2026-11-12 · [CORR] Second review of Paper Plan v3: the single-prefix shared-only arm could not fail (now M tenant prefixes); P0's novelty sentence rewritten and Lu et al.'s loads checked; units no longer mixed; the related-work sentence overclaimed absence; the reading caveat was stale
- **Source:** a second review of `docs/paper/paper-plan-v3.md`, passed on by the owner on 2026-11-12, and one more targeted re-read of Lu et al. through a fetch agent (verbatim for its abstract to §7.1; §7.2–§10 summary only). The errors are the agent's.
  1. **The shared-only arm as designed earlier today could not come out negative** (decisions entry "Design choices", item 3: one 2576-token prefix shared by all sessions). Every request would read that prefix, so some running request always holds it; a held block is not in the free queue and cannot be evicted (SOURCE(vLLM 0.32.0 v1/core/block_pool.py:get_new_blocks), open-questions S9). "No stuck run" would follow from the construction. **Replaced by:** M tenant prefixes of 2576 tokens each, every turn one tenant's prefix plus 496 fresh tokens, M set so that M × 2576 equals L1's warm working set at the test load (`derived.working_set` on the L1 control), popularity uniform, with a skewed variant as a harsher second case. Any tenant's prefix can then be evicted, so the arm can fail; what still differs from L1 is that a backlog adds no prefixes and waiting does not lengthen a prefix's idle time. The mean prompt (3072), mean uncached tokens (496), hit rate (0.8385) and output tokens (128) stay matched; the per-turn spread does not, and it is registered as a difference together with M and the popularity law. K2's claim wording follows: "a fixed set of prefixes shared across sessions" in place of "one system prompt shared by all sessions". M and the popularity law are not fixed here; they are for the registration.
  2. **P0's sentence on what is new did not parse and claimed more than was checked.** It read as if the stricter test applied to persistence, and "no burst test starts below 1.35" covered only two of the three papers. Checked now (BELIEF, fetch agent's verbatim quotes): Lu et al. give loads only against the warm overload rate, a +300 % surge trapping from 0.46–0.70 of it (their §4.1), and no all-miss capacity in session units, so they cannot be placed on the all-miss scale. The plan now states the comparison per paper in its own units and keeps only the two-sided statement: this study's cell is nearer the warm capacity (2.0 / 2.4 = 0.83, DERIVED, against at most 0.70) than any burst test in the three, and nearer the cold floor (1.19 against at least 1.35) than any that reports it.
  3. **Units were mixed in one sentence:** Huang and Liu's 2.7–3.1 is relative to their drain break-even, not to an all-miss capacity. Now stated apart.
  4. **"None reports the conditions under which the failure does not occur" was an overclaim.** Huang and Liu report no second state with caching off and none under a session cap; Valse and Jannesari report bursts of 25 and 40 sessions absorbed and a window too narrow to test; Lu et al. report a +33 % surge absorbed. The plan's sentence now lists these and limits the gap to: no paper varies turn semantics or reuse structure, or tests inside a narrow window. The earlier chat summaries that said "nobody says when it does not happen" were wrong in the same way.
  5. **Stale text in the plan:** the reading caveat (now says what was checked and how), three [VERIFY] tags on items since checked, and "loads well above the cold capacity". The review's item on step 4 ("one setup with a shared system prompt") had already been changed.
  6. **Ranges without their runs:** 1.03–1.08 times the floor covers REG-14 (λ = 2.2, 1.73–1.81 req/s) and REG-17 (λ = 2.0, 1.73–1.77); the shortfall is 11.5–13.5 % at 2.0 and 18–21 % at 2.2 (DERIVED: 1 − 1.81 / 2.2 = 0.177, 1 − 1.73 / 2.2 = 0.214). The review's 9.2–13.5 % applies REG-14's 1.81 to λ = 2.0, which is not a measured pair.
  7. **Unsourced sentence:** "a shared prompt is how many deployments get their hits" is now marked as needing a source.

## 2026-11-12 · [CORR] Lu et al. read directly: their simulated map reaches the warm overload rate, so "nearer the warm capacity than any burst test in the three" was wrong; their two unidentified references are identified
- **What was done:** the owner installed a PDF tool, and the agent read arXiv 2611.02543v1 itself, all 19 pages with figures and the reference list. It is the first of the three preprints read without a fetch agent in between. Statements about it are still BELIEF in rule B's sense (a paper is not one of the evidence tags), but they no longer rest on relayed quotes.
- **Error (the agent's):** the second [CORR] of today and the plan's P0 said this study's cell is "nearer the warm capacity (0.83 against at most 0.70) than any burst test in the three". Lu et al.'s Fig. 7 maps base loads from 0.4 to 1.0 of the steady-state overload rate, and their §4.1 says that as the base load approaches that rate the surge needed falls to +50 % (1P3D) and +25 % (GPU-only 1P1D). The 0.46–0.70 figure is the trapping load under a +300 % surge only. The sentence had been quoted to the agent by the fetch agent and was misread. **Corrected statement:** the cell is nearer the cold floor (1.19 against at least 1.35) than any burst test that reports that ratio, and it is a real-engine test in a narrow window on one colocated GPU; entry close to the warm capacity is already shown by Lu et al. in simulation. Their vulnerability maps, the 36-deployment comparison and the post-surge interventions are simulation (their §9, "Evaluation scope"); their real-engine motivating load (3.3 sessions/min) is given against neither capacity.
- **Confirmed by the direct read:** the §9 sentences used for K1 and K2 ("The feedback follows from closed-loop sessions, continuing arrivals and context-dependent miss cost"; independent sessions only; shared pages "contribute once to their aggregate footprint"; colocated deployments discussed, not evaluated); the trapped / overloaded definitions (§7.1); hardware on SGLang only; no code or data statement anywhere in the paper.

- **Correction to the fourth [CORR] (item 4):** the first-order estimate there holds for sessions (exact model: sessions at 0.89 of the all-miss capacity at ρ = 1.19, 0.83 at 1.31, 0.78 at 1.43; session backlog growing at 1.56, 1.53, 1.51 times the excess load). But "a request rate of 1.03–1.08 times the floor is expected as well" was too generous: the model's request rate is 1.016, 1.025 and 1.034 times the all-miss request rate at those loads, i.e. 1.71, 1.72 and 1.74 req/s against the open-loop floor of 1.681, while the measured span rates are 1.73–1.77 at λ = 2.0 and 1.73–1.81 at 2.2 (decisions.md 2026-11-10 [RESULT] REG-17 and REG-14). The measurements lie 1–5 % above the model's long-run value. Two explanations: the open-loop floor is a few percent low for closed-loop cells (Valse and Jannesari report their own reference rate 2–5 % short of saturation), or the runs are in the transient the model does not describe (theirs were about 10 % from the limit in the registered window). In model F the turn count does not change the trapped state much at a given ρ; what it should change is where the two capacities lie, which the model does not give. Metronome's "metastable" collapse is pool exhaustion by pinned, growing per-session state in speech serving, and its stall "never recovers, because audio keeps arriving open-loop": the opposite dependence on open-loop arrivals from K1's, in a system with no reusable prefix; K1's text now cites and separates it. VAMP reports an eviction and re-prefill cascade in closed-loop agent runs; MISA-T is a cap controller. None of the passages shows same-load history dependence. A full read of each is still owed before citing.
- **H2:** a one-dimensional diffusion of the KV demand that predicts the from-empty edge; by its authors' account pessimistic at the 300k pool on fresh seeds, one grid step high on vLLM, two steps low at 150k. K4's rationale in the paper plan now says so.

## 2026-11-12 · [DECISION] CLAUDE.md brought in line (owner approved); the stuck regime is called metastable, not bistable; K2 loses its shared-prefix half and is tested by the turn count alone
- **Owner (2026-11-12):** "resolve them", on the items the audit left open; then, on the three proposed edits to `CLAUDE.md`, "Alright do it, the reg 19 is currently on another sessions work, do else". The two wording and design choices below are the agent's under that delegation; the owner can reverse either.
- **`CLAUDE.md`, three lines changed as proposed:** the scope line ("the stuck state: reproducing it and mapping where it occurs; plan revised 2026-11-12"); the claims line ("C1–C2, now a cited premise, and K1–K5"); fixed choice 2 ("open-loop session arrivals (turn release, open- or closed-loop, is set per config and registered) … no KV offload, and no KV sharing between replicas"). The old wording "open-loop arrivals" contradicted every cell since REG-11, which the owner approved with closed-loop turns (decisions.md 2026-11-09 [REG] REG-11).
- **Wording: "metastable", not "bistable".** The stuck runs have a growing waiting line (76 → 120 in REG-17, decisions.md 2026-11-10 [RESULT]), so the degraded regime is not a second steady state; Valse and Jannesari make the same choice for the same reason (BELIEF). "Two states at one load" in PROTOCOL §3, condition 6, is kept as written and read as a healthy steady state and a self-sustaining degraded regime (`docs/definitions.md`, metastable failure). The related-work draft is reworded; "bistable" stays only for cited systems with two steady states. Alternative rejected: keeping "bistable", which claims a stationarity no run here shows.
- **K2: the shared-prefix half is dropped.** Reason (sixth [CORR] of today): with about 12 shared prefixes and about 65 requests running in the cold state, every prefix is held and cannot be evicted, so the arm could not get stuck and could not refute the claim; a catalog large enough to leave prefixes idle does not fit a 96,656-token pool at a matched cache gain (DERIVED: 96,656 / 2576 ≈ 37 prefixes at most). The paper states the shared-prefix case as a consequence of the engine's rule and cites what exists (Huang and Liu's collapsed hit ratio equal to their shared prompt; Valse and Jannesari's unproven expectation; both BELIEF). K2 is now: the vulnerable range widens with the turns per session, tested at 16 turns, then 4, against 8. This removes one setup (about 12–17 GPU h by the plan's estimate) and leaves K2 with one risky test. Alternative rejected: keeping the arm as a demonstration, which costs GPU time and can change no decision (rule A1).
- **Read for this entry (BELIEF):** Schroeder, Wierman and Harchol-Balter, NSDI 2006, §2 and §6: closed, open and partly open systems; principle (vii), a partly open system behaves like an open one at up to about 5 requests per session and like a closed one from about 10; principle (viii), think time has little effect on mean response time there. The turn counts 4, 8 and 16 straddle that rule of thumb, which K2's text now notes.
- **Spot check of an older result against its run folders** (the audit had not done one): RUN(20261110-182920_burst_l1pl350cl_r2.0_s2, gate.reg17_gate) gives span completion rates 1.773 and 1.733 req/s in the first two spans, `holds: True`, end queue slope 0.061 /s; RUN(20261110-174432_stage2_control_l1pl350cl_r2.0_s2, gate.reg17_gate) gives `tipped: False`. These match the REG-17 result as reported. One result checked, not all.
- **Changed:** `CLAUDE.md`; `docs/claims.md` (K2); `docs/definitions.md` (metastable failure, shared-only); `docs/experiment-plan.md` (step E, the map, the done list, the answered question); `docs/status.md` (the paper-layer paragraph and not-yet-done list for K2; three stale lines: two run counts and the 420 W line; a note in Sync that the Mac is ahead of the VM by document-only commits); `docs/open-questions.md` (A16); the local paper files.

## 2026-11-12 · [DECISION] K2 staged: the range is measured by sweeps first, against a prediction and a gate registered beforehand, and the 16-turn shock matrix runs only if the range widens; the L1 closed-loop cache-off sweep is run in any case
- **Owner (2026-11-12):** approved the agent's plan, which proposed this change (entry above).
- **Why:** K2 cost 12–17 GPU h per setup in the plan with no stop before the shock matrix, while the published model gives 16-turn sessions almost the same trapped state as 8-turn ones (`docs/model.md` M5) and the plan's case for the 16-turn setup rests on the prefill-token gap alone (6.2 → 10.9; `docs/experiment-plan.md`, answered questions). K2's first half, that the range from the cold floor to the warm capacity widens with the turns per session, is a statement about capacities, so sweeps alone can refute it. Also, K2 needs an 8-turn reference measured the same way, and the only L1 cold floor on record (1.681 req/s) was measured with open-loop turns.
- **What changes (`docs/experiment-plan.md` step E, mirrored in `docs/claims.md` K2):** E0 (0 GPU h) registers a numeric prediction of each setup's window ratio and the gate factor before any sweep (rule G); E1 (about 2.3 GPU h) is a closed-loop cache-off sweep at L1, run whatever step B finds (it also gives K3 its closed-loop floor; the answered question on the floor is amended); E2 (about 4.5 GPU h) are the 16-turn sweeps with caching on and off; the 16-turn shock matrix (about 8–12 GPU h) runs only if the 16-turn ratio passes the gate; 4 turns only after that. A range that does not widen is reported as refuting K2's first half for these setups.
- **Known weakness, to be stated in each registration:** the closed-loop warm capacity is surge-sensitive (decisions.md 2026-11-10 [CORR]), so every setup uses the same capacity rule on the same seed 0, and the ratio compares setups under one rule rather than measuring a sustained capacity.
- **Alternative rejected:** run the 16-turn shock matrix directly, as planned. It spends 8–12 GPU h on a setup whose premise (a wider range) could be refuted for about 4.5 h.
- **Not changed:** any run, config, check, threshold or code; each stage still needs its own `[REG]` and the owner's approval.

- **Open arm A:** `configs/burst_l1pl350ol_r2.0_w3000_s{15..19}.yaml`. Each extends its REG-19 partner and sets `workload.sessions.closed_loop: false`, the only change; the planned schedule is identical (the duration stays 4080 s, because `harness/workload.py` `_poisson_times` draws the Poisson count from rate × duration first). `tests/test_k1.py` checks schedule and resolved-config identity for every pair.
- **Drift check:** `configs/burst_l1pl350cl_r2.0_w3000_s15_drift.yaml`, REG-19's seed-15 closed burst run under a new name, run after arm A's third run. `k1.drift` compares its readout with the original's; a disagreement is reported with the result and changes no label (review, recommendation 9).
- **Controls, conditional:** `configs/stage2_control_l1pl350ol_r{2.0,2.5}_w3000_s{n}.yaml`, run only for an open seed whose burst run is cold-backlogged, right after it, to separate overload of the open-loop warm state from a stuck state. A recovered open run carries its own pre-burst baseline.
- **Open arm B (headroom check):** `configs/burst_l1pl350ol_r2.5_w3000_s{15,16,17}.yaml`, arm A's burst runs at λ = 2.5 (= 0.83 × 3.0), the burst unchanged; margin over the open-loop cold floor 2.5 / 1.681 = 1.49 (DERIVED), so by M2 a stuck state is possible there. Runs only if arm A gives `supports` or `supports_no_mechanism` (`k1.b_may_start`).
- **Order:** arm A in REG-19's run order (15–19), the drift run after the third; arm B seeds 15, 16, 17.
- **Standing instructions** as for REG-17 to REG-19: 350 W read before every launch; idle GPU ≤ 45 °C; clean tree at the registered commit; one rerun of a run invalid by the automatic checks; stop and ask on a client error, a burst that does not fill the pool, or an unexpected pre-launch check. **Added pre-launch read for the open arm:** `ulimit -n` in the shell that starts the harness; a stuck open-loop run can hold ≈ 960 open requests (DERIVED: (2.0 − 1.681) × 3000 s), each on its own connection (`loadgen_force_close`), and a descriptor limit near that ends the run in client errors (review, T3). If the limit is below 4096, stop and ask.

### Readout (`analysis/k1.py`, `cold_backlogged`; `docs/definitions.md`, cold-backlogged)
In the end window [3480, 4080) s against the baseline [300, 900) s:
- **reuse** (Σ cached tokens / Σ previous-turn prompt tokens over ok later turns whose first token falls in the window) ≤ baseline − 0.06 (`stuck_hit_drop`). Not the server hit rate: with closed-loop turns a backlog shifts the served mix towards first turns, which never hit, so the hit rate also measures the mix (review, T1). This statistic is new; the number is the verdict's;
- mean server waiting > baseline + 1.0 (`recovered_q_excess`);
- mean KV ≥ 0.9 (`gate.SURGE["kv_onset"]`; there applied to a 60 s rolling mean, here to the window's mean, a different statistic with the same number).
**Recovered** = reuse ≥ baseline − 0.06 and waiting ≤ baseline + 1.0 (the `recovered` rule's reuse and queue parts). A run that is neither is `partial_open` and cannot count towards `supports` (review, T2). No latency enters either readout.
**Mechanism** (`k1.mechanism`, [burst end, burst end + 600) s): shown when `gate.overlap_share` > 0.5 (REG-7's rule) **and** later turns whose first token came before the previous turn's end reuse more of their prefix than those after it. The overlap share before the burst is reported as a reference (review, recommendation 6).
**Reported, never deciding** (`k1.readouts`): `gate.shock_size`, the first-turn share of completions in the end window (`gate.turn0_share`), and the mean number of sessions in service before the burst and in the end window.
**Open-arm labels** (`k1.open_seed`): `recovered_open`, `partial_open`, `stuck_open` (cold, control warm), `overload_open` (both cold), `pending_control`, `cold_control` (cold, control unreadable), `lost_open` (burst run invalid after its rerun), `unclear` (a NaN readout), `not_run`. `lost_open` and `cold_control` count as cold: a stuck open-loop run is the likeliest to fail its checks (review, T3).

### Decision (`k1.k1_outcome`, paired by seed; the owner chose the exact one-sided McNemar test, 2026-11-12, over pooled Fisher; Fisher's p is reported beside it)
| Outcome | Rule, in this order | Decision that follows |
|---|---|---|
| `too_few` | fewer than 2 seeds with a reading in both arms | report; no K1 statement |
| `pending_controls` | an open cold run without its control | run the control, then compute again |
| `open_arm_overload` | an open run and its control both cold | the open-loop cell is not warm-healthy; K1 not testable there; owner decides |
| `closed_not_cold` | no closed run cold-backlogged | K1 not testable at REG-19's cell (the gate makes this unreachable) |
| `refutes` | `stuck_open` + `lost_open` + `cold_control` ≥ 3 | K1 reported as refuted at this cell and leaves the paper's core claims |
| `supports` | McNemar p ≤ 0.05, every non-cold open run `recovered_open`, mechanism shown in each | K1 stated for this cell with its mechanism; arm B starts |
| `supports_no_mechanism` | the same, mechanism not shown in every one | K1's outcome stated without "held prefix" as shown; arm B starts |
| `inconclusive` | otherwise | report; owner chooses between paired seeds 20+ and dropping K1 as a core claim |

Arm B (`k1.b_outcome`): `headroom_weakened` if all 3 seeds are `recovered_open`; `headroom_open` if any is cold, lost or partial (K1's wording then states the confound); `incomplete` otherwise. Three seeds are weak evidence: at a true cold rate of 0.4 all three recover with probability 0.22 (review, DERIVED).

### Prediction (BELIEF)
- Gate: each closed burst run cold-backlogged at 3000 s ≈ 0.85 (REG-17/18: 5 of 5 at 1500 s, RUN(20261110-182920_burst_l1pl350cl_r2.0_s2, k1.cold_backlogged) and the four REG-18 burst runs, reuse 0.000 at the end against ≈ 1.0 before; checked as a code smoke test on reported runs); REG-19 runs all five seeds ≈ 0.5. So arm A starts ≈ 0.2 (0.5 × 0.85⁵).
- Given arm A runs: each open run cold ≈ 0.10, partial ≈ 0.03, recovered ≈ 0.87 (REG-10: open-loop at 2.4 fully back within 393 s; RUN(20261108-220248_burst_l1pl350_r2.4_s1, k1.cold_backlogged) not cold, recovered); mechanism shown in every recovered run ≈ 0.8 (REG-10: overlap 0.835 after the burst, 0.502 before; reuse held 1.000 against idle 0.839, RUN(20261108-220248_burst_l1pl350_r2.4_s1, k1.mechanism)). Outcomes: `supports` ≈ 0.40, `supports_no_mechanism` ≈ 0.10, `inconclusive` ≈ 0.49, `refutes` ≈ 0.01 (DERIVED from those beliefs: 0.87⁵ = 0.50 for all five recovered; P(≥ 3 cold) = 0.009).
- Arm B, each seed cold ≈ 0.15; `headroom_weakened` ≈ 0.6.

### Alternatives to state with any result
1. **Working set, not held prefixes:** with closed-loop turns each session's lifetime grows by its turn latencies, so sessions in service and their distinct prefixes grow with the slowdown (REG-17/18 burst runs: 12–14 in service before the burst, 149–226 at the end; RUN(<run>, k1.readouts) on the five runs above, a smoke check). That is still turn semantics, but not the held-prefix mechanism. The mechanism contrast and the sessions-in-service readout separate them only partly; the wording of any `supports` says which was shown.
2. **Headroom:** arm B, at the same share of the warm capacity.
3. **Different shock:** the burst meets a different server state in each arm, by design; shock size is reported per arm.
4. **Different load under slowdown:** open-loop turns keep the offered load at λ while closed-loop turns lower it; an open arm that recovers does so under more load, which works against K1, not for it.
5. **Time and machine drift:** the closed arm ran days before; the drift run checks one seed.
6. **Selection by REG-19's stop:** its futility stop decides whether arm A can start at all.

### Cost
≈ 1.07–1.23 GPU h per 4080 s run (REG-19's estimate). Arm A 5 runs + drift 1 ≈ 6.4–7.4 h, only if the gate passes; arm B 3 runs ≈ 3.2–3.7 h, only after `supports`; ≈ 1.1 h per conditional control. Expected ≈ 0.2 × 7 + 0.1 × 3.5 ≈ 1.8 GPU h at today's beliefs; at most ≈ 19 h.

### Adversarial review (separate subagent; it saw only the first draft, its diff, the code and configs those call; it opened no runs and no docs). Verbatim:
> **1. Traces on which the label is wrong**
> - **T1 — `supports` with no cold cache in the closed arm (most likely trace).** Every session has its own random system prompt (`harness/workload.py:97`), so turn 0 can never hit. In the closed arm turn 0 is still released open-loop at λ/8 (`harness/loadgen.py:158-165`) while later turns slip behind the server. If the post-burst completion rate is below λ, live sessions pile up and the served mix shifts toward early turns. Healthy token-weighted hit ≈ 20608/24576 = 0.84 (computed from the schedule); serving one extra turn-0 per ~3 sessions puts the hit rate under 0.78 and fires `hit_cold`, while every later turn still gets ~95 % of its prefix. Add waiting 6 vs 0.3 baseline and KV 0.93 → closed run cold-backlogged, 5/5. The open arm, which cannot change its mix that way, recovers on headroom (0.67 of capacity): hit 0.83, q 0.2, KV 0.55; overlap share ≈ 0.55 just because e2e ≈ the mean 5 s gap (with e2e ≈ 3.5–4 s, P(gap < e2e) ≈ 0.5). Result: `supports` with mechanism, p = 0.004, and no cold cache or held prefix has been shown. The hit part of the readout is *not* "defined alike in both arms": in the closed arm it also measures request mix.
> - **T2 — `recovered_open` that is not recovered.** `recovered_open` only means "not all three parts" (`k1.py:56-60, 88`). An open run with queue 200, KV 0.95 and a hit drop of 0.05, or with KV 0.89, counts as recovered and toward `supports`.
> - **T3 — the open arm's failures are the likeliest runs to be lost.** A stuck open run grows an unbounded queue: about 0.32 req/s × 3000 s ≈ 960 outstanding requests (using the 1.681 floor), each holding its own socket (`loadgen.py:135`, `force_close`, `limit=0`). With a 1024 file-descriptor limit (BELIEF, unchecked) that gives `client_error`; busy-server scrapes over 0.9 s count as `failed_scrapes` and fail `recorder` (`harness/checks.py:87-98`). Invalid → one rerun → invalid → `reg20_table` drops the seed silently (`k1.py:153`). The closed arm's queue is bounded by live sessions and never meets this. So stuck open runs are filtered out, which biases toward `supports`. Same for an open control with a NaN window: it becomes `unclear` and the seed is dropped (`k1.py:95`).
> - **T4 — `refutes` from tiny counts.** k_c = 1 and k_o = 1 (n = 5 or n = 2) gives "refuted, leaves core claims" from one event per arm, with no test.
>
> **2. Bugs and mismatches**
> - **Pattern bug (`k1.py:37`).** `f"{2.0:g}"` gives `"2"`, so `open_pattern(2.0, s)` is `*_burst_l1pl350ol_r2_w3000_s15` and can never match `..._r2.0_...`. Arm A and its controls are never found, and `reg20_table` always returns `too_few`. No test calls `open_pattern`, `closed_pattern` or `reg20_table`.
> - Decision table: "supports → arm B may start", but `b_may_start` (`k1.py:136`) also requires `k_open == 0`, so 5/5 vs 1/5 (`supports`, tested at `test_k1.py:115`) blocks B; and `closed_not_cold` *does* let B start, although K1 cannot be tested there.
> - Alternative 2 promises `gate.shock_size` per arm; `k1.py` neither computes nor reports it.
> - The draft says dropped seeds are "reported". The code returns only a count (`dropped_unclear`), and seeds missing in either arm are skipped with no record (`k1.py:153-154`).
> - "None is new" is not quite true: `SURGE["kv_onset"]` (0.9) was registered as an onset on a 60 s rolling KV level (`gate.py:1347`); here it is applied to a 600 s window mean, a different statistic.
> - Fisher ignores the pairing. The seeds are paired (same schedule), but Fisher treats the arms as independent. 4/5 vs 0/5 gives Fisher p = 0.024, while the exact McNemar on 4 discordant pairs gives 0.0625. Rule H requires the pooling assumption to be stated.
> - "Same schedule" holds only for planned times. Realized pre-burst arrivals and live-session counts differ between arms, so the burst meets a different state by design. The closed arm also ran days earlier, so machine drift is confounded with the loop flag.
>
> **3. Strongest alternative for the likely result (open recovers, closed cold)**
> The closed loop inflates the working set. Each session's lifetime grows by the sum of its turn latencies, so live sessions, and their distinct prefixes, grow with the slowdown (Little's law) and overflow the 96,656-token pool; the hit-rate fall is partly the mix effect of T1. That is a turn-semantics effect, but not the "held prefix" mechanism K1 states. The design does not separate the two: overlap share > 0.5 is close to guaranteed in any open run with e2e near 5 s, there is no pre-burst reference or contrast against cold runs, and arm B tests headroom only, not working set or mix.
>
> **4. Can the run change a decision? Is an outcome foregone?**
> Yes in principle: `supports`, `refutes` and `inconclusive` lead to different actions. But k_c is known from REG-19 before arm A runs, and it settles what arm A can reach. `supports` needs k_c ≥ 4 of 5, or k_c = n at n = 3 or 4. Below that, only `inconclusive` or a rare `refutes` remains (at k_c = 3 of 5, P(`refutes`) ≈ 0.01–0.17 under the draft's open-arm rates) for ≈ 6 GPU h. If k_c = 0, `closed_not_cold` is certain and arm A cannot change anything, yet the draft still runs it, and then arm B. The mechanism clause is close to foregone. Arm B's 3 seeds are weak: at a true cold rate of 0.4, all three recover with P = 0.22, and nothing is tested.
>
> **5. Recommended changes (most important first)**
> 1. Fix `open_pattern` (format λ as `r2.0`); add a test that runs `reg20_table` on fake run folders.
> 2. Gate arm A on REG-19's closed count: register, before running, the k_c below which arm A is skipped (because `supports` is unreachable and refutation unlikely).
> 3. Replace the hit part with a per-turn measure that ignores the mix, e.g. the median of `cached_tokens / previous prompt_len` over later turns in the end window, in both arms. Report the turn-0 share (`gate.turn0_share`) per arm.
> 4. Require `recovered_open` to pass the actual `recovered` rule (hit and queue); anything in between is its own label that does not count toward `supports`.
> 5. Pre-register that an open seed lost to invalidity, or an `unclear` open control, counts as cold (or blocks `supports`). Check `ulimit -n` and scrape latency under an open-loop backlog before running.
> 6. Make the mechanism readout a contrast: the overlap share before the burst as a reference, plus the cached share of overlapped against non-overlapped later turns (`derived.cached_share_split`). Report the realized live-session working set per arm against pool size.
> 7. Use an exact paired test (McNemar on discordant pairs), or state why Fisher may pool the seeds.
> 8. Require k_c ≥ 2 and a test for `refutes`. Align `b_may_start` with the decision table and drop `closed_not_cold` from it. Implement `shock_size`.
> 9. Add one rerun of a closed seed, interleaved with arm A, as a drift check (≈ 1.1 h).

### Changed because of it
1. **The pattern bug was the agent's error** and would have made every computation return `too_few`: fixed (`r{lam:.1f}`), with tests that match the patterns to the config names and run `reg20_table` end to end on fake run folders, an invalid attempt and a drift run included.
2. Arm A is gated on REG-19's closed arm (`k1.a_may_start`).
3. The hit part is replaced by the prefix reuse of later turns (token-weighted, like the hit rate, rather than a median); the first-turn share is reported. On the five reported closed burst runs at λ = 2.0 the reuse is 0.000 at the end, so T1 did not occur there; the readout is chosen so it cannot occur.
4. `recovered_open` needs the `recovered` rule's reuse and queue parts; `partial_open` is its own label and blocks `supports`.
5. `lost_open` and `cold_control` count as cold; a `ulimit -n` read is added before the open runs. Scrape latency under an open-loop backlog is not tested beforehand (no cheap test without the GPU); a `recorder` failure makes the run `lost_open` after its rerun, which counts against K1.
6. The mechanism is a contrast (held against idle reuse) with the pre-burst overlap reported; sessions in service are reported per arm. The pool-size comparison is left to the result text.
7. The paired McNemar test is primary, the owner's choice; Fisher's p is reported beside it.
8. `refutes` needs 3 open seeds stuck, lost or with an unreadable control (an event count, not a test; one event per arm no longer refutes); `b_may_start` follows the table; `shock_size` is reported.
9. The drift run is added.
- **Not changed:** the KV threshold keeps the number 0.9 on a window mean, now stated as a different statistic; the different realized pre-burst state between arms is stated as alternative 3, not removed (it is what the loop flag does).
- **Code and configs:** `analysis/k1.py` (new), `analysis/stats.py` (`fisher_one_sided`), `tests/test_k1.py` (50 tests), 17 configs (`configs/*_l1pl350ol_*`, 16; `configs/burst_l1pl350cl_r2.0_w3000_s15_drift.yaml`). No harness, check, threshold or `uv.lock` change. `docs/definitions.md` gains "cold-backlogged".
- **Status:** a draft. Nothing runs before the owner approves it, and the gate is computed only after REG-19's [RESULT].

## 2026-11-12 · [CORR] Lu et al. as the paper documents describe them: their real-engine trap load is given (half the profiled critical rate), the 0.46–0.70 sentence is in §4.2, and three related-work sentences misstated their tests
- **Source:** a second agent's reading of Lu et al. (arXiv 2611.02543), pasted by the owner on 2026-11-12 as proposed edits PP1–PP5 and RW1–RW4. Each claim was checked by this agent against the arXiv v1 PDF (session scratchpad, `pdftotext`, page read for the section). Statements about the paper stay BELIEF in rule B's sense. 0 GPU h; no run data.
- **Errors (the agent's, in `docs/paper/paper-plan-v3.md` and `docs/paper/related-work-approach-v3.md`, both local; the quote check of rows 8–20 earlier today missed the first two):**
  1. **"Lu et al.'s real-engine load is not given against either capacity."** Wrong. Their hardware runs replay the simulated arrival schedules (§7.1, p. 10), whose main comparison "starts at half the deployment's profiled critical rate and applies a ×5 surge"; HiCache "remains trapped in all four" real H200 1P3D scenarios (§7.2, p. 11). Whether the profiled critical rate equals their steady-state overload rate is not stated.
  2. **Location of "between 0.46 and 0.70 of the steady-state overload rate":** §4.2 ("More Cache Moves the Boundary"), not §4.1. The surge sizes near overload (+50 %, +25 %) are in §4.1.
  3. **"Terminating the sessions left over from the surge restores service within minutes."** That test is separate from the +100 % surge: a burst of short sessions at four times the base rate, and terminating the burst sessions "restores service within two minutes" (§3.3, pp. 3–4).
  4. **"an admission design that they evaluate on SGLang and in a calibrated simulator."** The design, BASIN, combines a fixed session priority, decode-memory lending, admission and shedding; only a partial, arrival-time prototype runs on SGLang, and the full predictor-driven policy only in simulation (§1, p. 2; §7.2, p. 11).

## 2026-11-12 · [DECISION] A14 fixed: the recorder can no longer die on a half-written line, run.py logs its death, and the `recorder` and `gpu_steady` checks need coverage (checks only get stricter)

- **Cause (BELIEF; the traceback was lost):** `LagTail.recent_max` parsed every line it read with `json.loads`, including a final line the load generator was still writing, and moved its offset past it; that call and the GPU read sat outside the recorder loop's `try`, so one exception ended the process; `run.py` never polled the recorder and stopped it quietly at the end, so its death left no event (FILE(harness/recorder.py), FILE(harness/run.py)).

## 2026-11-12 · [DECISION] The session cap is built in the load generator (step D; a workload change approved by the owner), off unless a config sets `workload.sessions.cap`
- **Owner (2026-11-12):** "yes, go ahead with 2, 3 and 4"; item 4 was the session-cap arm's load-generator change. 0 GPU h. No capped config exists yet: the cap's value comes from the chosen cell's control after REG-19 (`docs/experiment-plan.md`, step D and the answered design question on the cap's value).
- **Built as defined** (`docs/definitions.md`, session cap): `workload.sessions.cap` (read with `.get`, absent or null = no cap, so every existing config is unchanged; refused at startup, before the server starts, with open-loop turns or a value that is not a positive integer); `harness/loadgen.py` `SessionCap`, an explicit first-come-first-served queue that hands a freed slot to the oldest waiter; `session_chain` waits for a slot at turn 0's planned time and holds it until the chain ends (last turn ended, failed, or cancelled at the deadline). Burst requests are not session chains and pass the cap. The gateway stays off.
- **Recorded:** turn 0 of a capped session carries `t_arrived` (reached the cap) and `t_admitted` (got a slot), and its `t_released` is the admission time, so latency (`load.load_run`, from `t_released`) and `client_lag` measure from admission, and the wait at the cap is reported apart (`cap.cap_wait`). Records without a cap are as before.
- **Checks:** `arrival_rate` counts a capped session's arrival at `t_arrived`, sent or not (a session still waiting at the deadline is counted where it arrived). `release_chain` needed no change: a never-admitted session's later turns have no previous end, which it already counts as blocked.
- **Analysis:** `analysis/cap.py`: `max_sessions_in_service` (the cap's value: exact maximum of sessions in service over a run, burst requests excluded, the same in-service definition as `k1.sessions_in_service`), `cap_wait`.
- **Tests:** `tests/test_session_cap.py` (14 with parameters: FIFO admission and slot hand-over; a cancelled waiter leaves the queue; the value must be a positive integer; config reading and the open-loop refusal; a chain waits, records arrival and admission, and turn 0 is released at admission; a slot is freed on failure and on cancellation, and a never-admitted session stays as a miss with its arrival; an end-to-end capped run against `tests/fake_vllm.py` with a burst is valid, never has more than 2 sessions in service, and sends the burst on time; the run is refused before the server starts with open-loop turns; the exact sweep; the wait summary). `tests/test_e2e_fake.py` unchanged and passing.
- **Not changed:** any used config, threshold or registered test; `docs/definitions.md` (session cap) gains its Code line.

Removed; 0.83 is kept as a fact about the cell.
- **Also added (verified):** Huang and Liu's platform (vLLM 0.20 on AMD MI300X, arms on separate GPUs, reproduced on SGLang; §3); Valse and Jannesari's trap rule at 9 of 10 rates, the 30 s tool slowdown trapping 1 of 3 runs, the arrival stop against the in-trap cap rescuing 9 of 9 (§1, §4, §5); model F's all-miss assumption ((F1), §3) and the units of λ_ref (turns-based, cache off, a closed population of 32, a hit meaning more than half the prompt cached; §2, §3, App. E.3) in K3; KAIROS §6.2.4 asserts persistence without a test that removes the cause; posting dates and the order of the three preprints (Valse and Jannesari App. E.1; Huang and Liu §7); arXiv versions and dates in the references; Huang and Liu's 0.035 paired / 0.04 other loads (0.80 is our arithmetic).
