## 2026-11-13 · [DECISION] A17 answered from the pinned source (the scheduler does not skip a head request that does not fit); analysis code now refuses run folders that a pending registration withholds (agent, within its authority)
- **A17 (0 GPU h, no run read).** Read: the v0.32.0 tag tarball of the source questions (sha256 `bf592c132f27bbb5f65cff0bbd2ee873eae722b79c8286934fd5b5cf88b43d61`, recomputed today; the extracted `scheduler.py` equals the tarball member). In `Scheduler.schedule` the waiting loop takes the head of the queue with `peek_request` and calls `allocate_slots(…, full_sequence_must_fit=self.scheduler_reserve_full_isl, …)`; when it returns `None` the loop ends with `break` (SOURCE(vLLM 0.32.0 v1/core/sched/scheduler.py:Scheduler.schedule), lines 1256–1282). A waiting request is passed over (`skip_request`, lines 904–910) only when it is blocked on remote KV, a grammar or streaming input, has stale output in flight after a preemption, meets the LoRA limit, has an undetermined connector match, or has an encoder transfer pending (lines 929–952, 986–991, 1070–1072, 1094–1096). In this study's runs only the stale-output case can occur: a preempted request is put back at the head (`prepend_request`, line 1613) and is passed over until its in-flight output has drained. The queue is a deque (SOURCE(vLLM 0.32.0 v1/core/sched/request_queue.py:FCFSRequestQueue)).
  - **So:** a head request that does not fit the KV pool blocks the line; an all-miss server admits in arrival order, except that preempted requests re-enter at the head. The E0/E1 review's worry (recommendation 9: an open-loop arm that leaves planned order) does not arise from this path. It bore only on E1's reported tilt, which is not judged.
  - **Limits:** the tarball, not the VM's wheel; read, not tested on a live server; "admits" is not "completes": chunked prefill and batching still interleave running requests.
  - **Changed:** `docs/open-questions.md` A17.
- **Withheld runs (code and tests; no run read).** New module `analysis/withheld.py`: a run folder is sealed from the moment it exists until this file holds the [RESULT] heading of the registration that owns it. While sealed, `load.load_run` raises `WithheldError`, and `load.find_runs`, `recheck.recheck`, `tables.arrival_table` and `engine_config.scan` skip it with a line on stderr. Seals today: REG-19 (`*_l1pl350cl_r2.0_w3000_s1[5-9]`, lifted by "[RESULT] REG-19") and REG-20 (its open-loop arms, their controls and the drift rerun, lifted by "[RESULT] REG-20"). The owning registration's own computation sets `AFTERSHOCK_UNSEAL=<id>`.
  - **Why:** `tables.py verdicts|sweeps|published`, `analysis.recheck "*"`, `gate.surge_table` and `k3`'s batch-1 finder (`find_runs("*_l1pl350cl_*")`, FILE(analysis/k3.py:381)) glob every run folder, so each would have read REG-19's six runs on record before its [RESULT]. With the seal these tools can be used on the other runs.
  - **Not covered, on purpose:** `checks.json`, which a rerun decision reads (REG-19's stopping rule), and `tools/` (checksums, validity flags, inventory).
  - **REG-19 itself is not touched by this change:** `analysis/gate.py` is unchanged, and REG-19's computations are to run from a worktree at `a7bb77a` (the resume decision, in review), whose code has no seal.
  - **Tests:** `tests/test_withheld.py`, 12: each seal covers exactly its registration's config names and no run on record; a seal lifts only on a `## ` heading; the variable names the registration; `load_run` refuses a sealed folder without reading it and `find_runs` skips it; `recheck` skips it.

  - REG-21: rule F round 16, NOT READY, required BA1–BA4 (FILE(docs/drafts/reviews-2026-11-13/rulef-reg21-draft23-r16.md:1)); owner-proxy REJECT of draft 23 as written, binding, conditions BB1–BB9 (the proxy's own reading: the reject is about batch 1's "What was known", not the two git facts).
  - REG-22: rule F round 9, NOT READY, required BC1–BC3 (FILE(docs/drafts/reviews-2026-11-13/rulef-reg22-draft14-r9.md:1)); owner-proxy APPROVE on BD1–BD9, with no effect while rule F is NOT READY.
- **The rule, as read here:**
  1. **Rounds counted** are those on the freeze design, per registration: round 1 = REG-21's rule F r16 / REG-22's r9 with their proxy passes (done); round 2 = r17 / r10; round 3 = r18 / r11. There is no round 4 on batch 2.

That text gets its own rule F review and owner-proxy pass, binding as always.
  5. **What "retrospective by design" computes** (BD8): batch 2 is still computed once, by the same command, after REG-19's final [RESULT], with the judged path frozen at the entry and the entry's decision lines; no code or threshold changes after the entry (rule A5 binds a retrospective batch too); what a retrospective batch 2 may say is set by each registration's own text (REG-21: it never governs, BB6; REG-22: it enters the disagreement test, BC1).   - For every folder under `runs/`, sorted by name, the script read `config.yaml` fields, `checks.json`'s `valid` and `failed`, the `no_errors` counts `ok` and `unfinished`, and the number of files.   - The last two folder names in `runs/` are seed 17's control `20261112-103423_stage2_control_l1pl350cl_r2.0_w3000_s17` and its burst run `20261112-135538_burst_l1pl350cl_r2.0_w3000_s17` (folder names, read today; nothing is ever removed from `runs/`, rule 4).
  - With the script's display options, `pandas`' `to_string` prints one line per row (DERIVED: on synthetic data, 5 rows of 26 columns gave 6 lines; pandas 3.1.0 in `.venv`).
  - So the three printed lines were most likely those two rows, `ok` and `unfinished` included, and a count line. This is DERIVED from the inputs; the output was not opened.
  - Ten seconds later the subagent blanked `ok` and `unfinished` for every `w3000` folder and ran the script again (PROBE(docs/probe/20261113_transcript_search/inputs_s57_inv.txt), line 43).

- **Why.** Rule F round 11's BK2 trace, step 8, ran fact (2)'s commands in a throwaway repository and wrote two table-file names with made-up stamps into its saved review (FILE(docs/drafts/reviews-2026-11-13/rulef-reg22-draft16-r11.md:74)). The exemption selects on no run data: it is fixed before any table file exists (fact (2)'s commands printed no table-file name on 2026-11-13 at 21:01 UTC, the dry run of the [DECISION] (delegate) entries' checks), it names the two stamps and nothing else, and a real file with either stamp still counts.

REG-22's owner-proxy approved it and asked for this entry, written as given, before E of either registration ("Written as given, this needs no further pass", FILE(docs/drafts/reviews-2026-11-13/proxy-reg22-draft18-delta.md:67)); REG-21's owner-proxy approved CG1 for REG-21 (FILE(docs/drafts/reviews-2026-11-13/proxy-reg21-draft27-delta.md:1), "CG1, cross-applied from REG-22's rule F round 12 (approve)").
- **Timing.** This entry is committed before E of either registration (BK-S1, FILE(docs/decisions.md:4549)); both [DECISION] (delegate) entries cite it.
- **Not changed:** any threshold, code, run set, label or other part of the review-stop rule.

## 2026-11-13 · [CORR] The agent let a subagent edit `analysis/e1.py` in the main checkout while REG-19's queue ran, and the queue's guard stopped it before seed 19's step; the agent also first watched for a queue line that is not an allowed read

- **What was wrong.** At 21:32:05 UTC the agent started a subagent to write E1's draft 6, with code changes to `analysis/e1.py`, in the main checkout and without a separate worktree. REG-19's queue was running and requires `analysis/` to equal HEAD before each step (FILE(docs/probe/20261113_reg19/ops_r3/common.sh:207)). The subagent's edit at 21:38 UTC stopped the queue before seed 19's step (the [OPS] above).
- **Effect.** A delay of about three minutes to the step, from the stop at 21:46 UTC to the restart at 21:48:38 UTC. No run was lost or launched, no step was computed twice, and nothing beyond the allowed lines was read. The guard worked as written.
- **A second, smaller error.** The first command the agent wrote to wait for the restarted queue's end also printed lines starting `RECHECK `, which are not among the queue's allowed lines. The agent stopped that command before the queue had printed anything: the command's output holds the file's path and `[killed]` only. It then waited with the allowed patterns alone. No `RECHECK` line was read.
- **Fix, from now on.** While a queue that guards `analysis/`, `harness/` or `configs/` is running, a subagent that edits code works in its own git worktree, or writes patch files only. A command that prints queue lines uses exactly the allowed patterns (`RUN … VALID/INVALID`, `COPIED`, `STEP after seed …`, `QUEUE …`).

### What it can and cannot show (rule A1)
- The label `loop` (a code label; see decision line c) says that, at the registered thresholds, **in every 300 s span after the burst's requests had left, the reuse of later turns stayed at least 0.06 below its baseline, the session uncached rate at least twice its baseline, and the pool full and the batch large.** It lets through: a span with the cache back for up to about 240 of 300 s while the pool stays full and the batch large (FILE(docs/drafts/reviews-2026-11-13/rulef-reg22-draft5-r3.md), trace t04); a full recovery of up to about 65 to 70 s; and spans in which up to about two thirds of later turns hit at the cold completion rates (FILE(docs/drafts/reviews-2026-11-13/rulef-reg22-draft4-r2.md), section 4; and R10 below). It does not say that the cache was lost in every second of every span. (Draft 6 said "no span re-warmed for most of its length"; that is false on t04. The words came from rule F round 2's N7; round 3's F2 corrects them.)
- **It does not say why.** A queue that the load alone sustains gets the same label: a queue fills a pool that holds about 30 requests, and a full pool evicts prefixes (DERIVED by rule F round 1 from the configs: 96,656 tokens of pool ÷ (3072 + 128) tokens per request at the mean prompt = 30.2; FILE(docs/drafts/reviews-2026-11-13/rulef-reg22-draft3-r1.md)). What separates a loop from an overload is PROTOCOL §3 conditions 2, 5 and 6 and the loop-cut controls, not this table. The same-seed control's values are reported beside each run for that reason.
- The four links rest on two independent facts, the reuse of later turns and KV. The running batch follows from KV, and the uncached rate follows from the reuse unless throughput falls below about half of the offered rate (DERIVED by rule F round 1, same file).
- **Batch 1 is close to decided before it is computed.** The published spans of every stuck run show hit 0.000, KV about 0.95 and about 30 running (see "What was known"). BELIEF: P(all eleven stuck runs `loop`) ≈ 0.8. **The likeliest outcome of batch 1, `loop` in all eleven, changes no decision.** P(any decision line below changes a decision, batch 1) ≈ 0.05 (BELIEF); P(the same, batch 2) ≈ 0.002 at the forecast and up to ≈ 0.08 at the pessimistic end (DERIVED under "Prediction": batch 2 computed ≈ 0.6 and with at least three stuck runs ≈ 0.7 of that, both BELIEF, times P(`not_sustained` in at least two of three stuck runs) ≈ 0.004 or ≈ 0.20: 0.6 × 0.7 × 0.004 ≈ 0.0017, 0.6 × 0.7 × 0.20 = 0.084). Batch 2 keeps outcomes that change a decision (line e), so it is registered; with probability about 0.87 or more neither batch changes one (DERIVED: 1 − 0.05 − 0.084), and its cost is a minute of CPU (rule A1). The outcomes that carry information are `not_sustained` and `undefined`; `not_memory_limited` would change a claim but is close to excluded for batch 1 by what is published.
- **New in batch 1 (BELIEF that none of it was computed before):** the reuse and the uncached rate per span, the span [1380, 1680) s of the twelve 1500 s runs, N per span for most runs, the exact exit, the onsets of the reuse, the uncached rate and N, and the onset reading (the KV onset is not new: `gate.kv_onset`, FILE(analysis/gate.py:1361), runs for every closed-loop run, and REG-17's was published as 965 s, FILE(docs/decisions.md:3541)), the eviction histograms, the same-seed controls' links.

### Scope
- **This registration covers computing and reporting only.** Every edit to `docs/claims.md` or `docs/paper/` that rests on it needs its own decision, rule F review and owner-proxy pass, and stays under the ceilings of the decision lines below. **An edit to PROTOCOL needs the owner;** it is not a delegate decision. `PROTOCOL.md` and `docs/experiment-plan.md` are not edited under REG-22, by note or by pointer. The registration of D1 and D2 needs its own decision.
- **Question:** in the burst runs that the registered verdict calls `stuck`, do condition 4's registered levels hold at the end of the watch (mean KV ≥ 0.80, mean running batch N ≥ 2 × its baseline, N below the 256 cap), and do the loop's four links (cache lost, prompts recomputed, large batch, full pool) hold together in every 300 s span once no burst request is left in the system?
- **Claim:** C2. Its test, its first sentence in full: "in stuck runs, the loop figure (helper metrics in the plan's order) and condition 4 (mean KV ≥ 0.80, mean N ≥ 2 × baseline, N below the 256 cap); then the controls that cut a link: prefix caching off, and a session-cap arm (a limit on the sessions in service, set at the load generator)" (FILE(docs/claims.md:25)). Its "Supports" line, in full: "stuck runs that show the order and the memory limit, and stop getting stuck when a link is cut" (FILE(docs/claims.md:26)). **REG-22 makes no loop figure** and runs no control that cuts a link.

### The order clause is not judged
- **REG-22 changes no rule.** PROTOCOL §3 condition 4 and C2's test in `docs/claims.md` stay as written, the order clause included ("and the traces follow the plan's order", FILE(docs/decisions.md:285)). REG-22 computes condition 4's registered levels and reports the onset order. It does not judge the order clause on any run.
- **`sustain` and the four labels are REG-22's own description.** That `sustain` could stand for the order clause on burst runs is a proposal to the owner. It is in force only after an entry headed `[DECISION] (owner)` says so. The reason for the proposal, BELIEF and untested: the plan's order (FILE(docs/experiment-plan.md:285)) describes a cache wipe, where the loss comes first; on a burst run the first events are the trigger's own (batch and KV up), so a literal order test would fail every burst run for a reason that says nothing about the loop. The onset reading below bears on this BELIEF (open question A19, added with this entry) only through the pairs (reuse, N) and (reuse, KV). The reuse and the uncached rate are read from the same turns, so the pair (reuse, uncached rate) is `together` under any step, and the run-level reading `plan_order_beyond_lags` cannot occur; a wipe in the plan's exact order reads `not_distinguishable_from_simultaneous`. The uncached rate is session work per second, which the burst dilutes while it shares the server, so its pairs can read `reversed` when all four step at once. Session signals are read by first token, so if session turns get no first token during the burst, the reuse, too, crosses only once they are served again, whenever the cache was lost (FILE(docs/drafts/reviews-2026-11-13/rulef-reg22-draft5-r3.md), traces t03b E and F, t03 C and C2; alternative 7). The pairs bear on A19 only where every trailing 60 s window through the burst held at least 20 later turns; REG-22 does not compute where that holds, so it leaves A19 open.
- **Until then no entry, status line, claims line, definition or paper text says that condition 4 is met, holds or is passed for any run or load,** with or without a qualifier. No REG-22 label is counted towards the six conditions of PROTOCOL §3. Below, "condition 4's registered levels" means `levels` and "the links in every judged span" means `sustain`; neither is called "condition 4".

### Statistic (`analysis/c2.py`)
Baseline: the 600 s before the burst starts, [300, 900) s in every config here. End window: the last 600 s of the watch (FILE(configs/stage2_cap_base.yaml:8)). Spans: the watch cut into 300 s spans from the burst's end (1080 s). Watches: 1500 s in twelve of the 13 batch-1 runs (ten of the eleven stuck ones), 4500 s in REG-15's run, 3000 s in REG-19's (DERIVED from FILE(configs/stage2_base.yaml:13) and FILE(configs/confirm_l1pl350cl_r2.2_s12.yaml:13); all multiples of 300). REG-15's watch ends at 5580 s, where its drop to λ = 1 begins (FILE(configs/confirm_l1pl350cl_r2.2_s12.yaml:10)), so all its spans are at λ = 2.2.
- **levels** (`c2.levels`, FILE(analysis/c2.py:85); thresholds of decisions.md 2026-11-01, FILE(docs/decisions.md:285)): in the end window, mean KV ≥ 0.80, mean N ≥ 2 × its baseline mean, maximum N < 256. The function names which failed. In this setup the cap cannot be reached (the pool holds at most about 42 requests at the smallest prompt, DERIVED by rule F, same file), and N ≥ 2 × baseline can fail only if the baseline N is above about 12 to 15 (DERIVED by rule F round 2: by tokens at the mean prompt, N is 24.2 at KV 0.80 and 28.7 at 0.95).
- **A gauge value needs coverage** (`c2.gauge`, FILE(analysis/c2.py:48)): scrapes within 10 s of each end of its window and no gap above 10 s (`load._covered`); otherwise the value is missing.
- **The exit** (`c2.last_burst_end`, FILE(analysis/c2.py:101)): the moment the last burst request ended. Missing if a burst request never ended, ended with an error status, or the run has no burst rows.
- **links** (`c2.links`, FILE(analysis/c2.py:111)), over one span:
  1. reuse of later turns (cached tokens over the previous prompt, by first token; at least 20 later turns, else missing) ≤ baseline − 0.06 (the verdict's `stuck_hit_drop`, 0.06 in every config). At full reuse this reuse is 1.0 (DERIVED from the session shape: a later turn's prefix is its previous prompt); the counter hit rate in the same warm state is about 0.84 (FILE(docs/decisions.md:3747)).
  2. session uncached prefill (prompt tokens not served from the cache, session requests only, per second, by first token) ≥ 2 × baseline;
  3. mean N ≥ 2 × baseline;
  4. mean KV ≥ 0.80.
  The function names the links that fail. Any missing value, the baseline's included, makes the span's result missing, never a failure. The uncached rate raises if an ok session request has no first-token time or prompt length; a request without `cached_tokens` counts as a full miss, and a request with a first token that never finished is not counted (both are counted and reported, `c2.row_counts`).
- **sustain** (`c2.sustain`, FILE(analysis/c2.py:125)): a span is judged when it starts at or after the exit. Every span of the watch is reported with that flag (the JSON prints it as the string "True" or "False"); the unjudged span that holds the exit mixes time before and after it.
- **What a link's threshold lets through.** A full recovery of up to about 65 to 70 s inside one span fails no link (the first failure comes by KV); the reuse link fails only at about 285 of 300 s with the cache back (DERIVED by rule F round 2 on a baseline of 1.0, E1 and E2). A re-warming span shows first in the uncached rate (FILE(tests/test_c2.py:62), `test_a_span_in_which_the_cache_comes_back_breaks_sustain`: on that test's baseline of 1.0, the cache back for 250 of 300 s gives reuse 0.83 and fails only link 2). So `loop` excludes a span with the cache back for more than about 240 of its 300 s, or with a full recovery of more than about 70 s, at 300 s resolution.
- **Why 2 × for the uncached rate (fixed before any run is read for it):** DERIVED from the L1 schedule. Warm, a session of 8 turns prefills 2176 + 7 × 256 = 3968 tokens; cold, 24,576. At equal request rates the cold rate is 6.2 × the warm one (DERIVED: 24,576 / 3968). At the cold completion rates on record (1.73 to 1.81 req/s, RUN(20261110-182920_burst_l1pl350cl_r2.0_s2, gate.reg17_gate), RUN(20261110-063647_burst_l1pl350cl_r2.2_s2, gate.reg14_gate)) against 2.0 to 2.4 req/s offered it is about 4.5 to 5.6 × (DERIVED). The link fails when the share of turns that hit reaches 0.81 at equal request rates (DERIVED: 24,576 − 20,608 h = 2 × 3968), and already at 0.66 to 0.77 at those cold completion rates (DERIVED by rule F round 1; reproduced in round 2).

### Labels (`c2.condition4`, FILE(analysis/c2.py:172))
In this order:
1. The levels cannot be read (a gauge does not cover the end window or the baseline): `undefined`.
2. The levels fail: `not_memory_limited`, whatever `sustain` is.
3. The levels hold and there are fewer than two judged spans (or no exit): `undefined`. One judged span that fails is still `undefined`.
4. The levels hold and a judged span fails a link: `not_sustained`, even if another judged span has a missing value.
5. The levels hold, no judged span fails, and one has a missing value: `undefined`.
6. Otherwise: `loop`.

Rule F round 2 checked these six cases against the code in 18 cells and found them equal (FILE(docs/drafts/reviews-2026-11-13/rulef-reg22-draft4-r2.md), section 2).

### Counts (rule H)
- Per load: k of n `loop` with its one-sided 95 % Clopper–Pearson lower and upper bounds (`stats.cp_upper`), never pooled across loads or batches. **A sentence about a load needs at least 3 stuck runs at it;** below that the runs are reported one by one.
- **The command prints two things used only as follows** (N1): a row for λ = 2.2 (n = 2, with bounds), which counts the 1500 s run and the 4500 s run together (4 and 14 spans), and an all-load `counts`. The 2.2 row is never quoted; the all-load `counts` is quoted only with the words "a tally, no bound; the eleven runs hold six distinct seeds" (seeds 1, 2, 3, 4, 6 at 2.4; 2 and 12 at 2.2; 2, 3, 4, 6 at 2.0).
- Among the stuck runs, seeds 2, 3, 4 and 6 were run at λ = 2.0 and 2.4 and seed 2 also at 2.2 (seed 5 was run at both 2.0 and 2.4, `bad_baseline` at both), and the schedules of one seed at two loads are nested (FILE(tests/test_k3w.py:438)): the loads' counts are paired by seed and are not independent samples. This is said beside any two loads' counts.

- **Their verdicts as published** (`load.verdict`):
  - λ = 2.4: `20261109-042828_burst_l1pl350cl_r2.4_s1` `stuck` (FILE(docs/decisions.md:2312)); `…_s2`, `…_s3`, `…_s4`, `…_s6` (`20261109-080203`, `-093609`, `-111316`, `-151300`) `stuck`, `20261109-125300_burst_l1pl350cl_r2.4_s5` `bad_baseline` (FILE(docs/decisions.md:2467) to FILE(docs/decisions.md:2471)).
  - λ = 2.2: `20261110-063647_burst_l1pl350cl_r2.2_s2` `stuck` (FILE(docs/decisions.md:2836)); `20261110-085730_confirm_l1pl350cl_r2.2_s12` `stuck` (FILE(docs/decisions.md:3088)).
  - λ = 2.0: `20261110-182920_burst_l1pl350cl_r2.0_s2` `stuck` (FILE(docs/decisions.md:3541)); `20261111-101805_…_s4`, `20261111-115409_…_s3`, `20261111-150642_…_s6` `stuck`, `20261111-133019_burst_l1pl350cl_r2.0_s5` `bad_baseline` (FILE(docs/decisions.md:3742) to FILE(docs/decisions.md:3745)).
  - So 11 `stuck` and 2 `bad_baseline`. The command recomputes the verdicts; a difference from this list is a deviation, reported first.
- **A run is judged only if its verdict is `stuck`;** the two `bad_baseline` runs are listed with their verdict. Both ended cold, full and backlogged by their [RESULT] entries (FILE(docs/decisions.md:2480), FILE(docs/decisions.md:3747)); they are left out because the claim's test says "in stuck runs", and that is said with the result.
- **Batch 2** (`c2.batch_runs(2)`, which is `k3w.batch2_runs`, FILE(analysis/k3w.py:341)): REG-19's burst runs, one valid run per seed, a prefix of seeds 15–19 and at least three. It raises before a line that begins as REG-19's result heading does is in `docs/decisions.md`; the guard is that no such line is written before REG-19's final result.
- **Batch 2 is not computed, and is reported as not computed with the reason,** in each of these cases: REG-19 ends without the table that `final.sh` saves (an operational stop, or spent attempts); the valid folders matching the batch-2 pattern (names and `valid` only, compared by name before the command runs) differ from the burst runs whose seeds are in n of that table as REG-19's final [RESULT] reports it; `batch_runs(2)` raises, for any reason; at or after S (the stopping rule's fact (2)) and before batch 2, an entry changes the seeds that table counts or the validity flag of a matching run (a flag set before S is part of what that table counts; an entry is placed by its commit's committer time, compared with S as instants, the same second counting as after). REG-22 is not withdrawn after this entry: once REG-19's final [RESULT] exists, batch 2 is computed or declared not computed by these rules. The comparison is against the seeds in n, so a seed that REG-19 excludes (`exposed` with outcome `control_cold_surge`, FILE(analysis/gate.py:1684)) but whose burst run is valid would end batch 2, as in REG-21; that case cannot arise, because no REG-19 seed is exposed ("No control reaches `surge_tip` 3.2 within 4080 s (highest 3.092), so no seed is exposed", FILE(docs/decisions.md:3788)). Batch 2 is also not computed if `reported_counts` raises during batch 2 (the stopping rule's last bullet), so that this list is complete in one place. No rule picks runs afterwards, and no folder, pattern, function or validity flag is changed to make the selection pass. The batches are reported apart and never pooled.

### What was known when the thresholds were fixed
Every batch-1 run has been reported, and every threshold here was fixed knowing these numbers. For batch 1 that makes this a retrospective reading that is never called a test (the study's standard: FILE(docs/experiment-plan.md:413), FILE(docs/claims.md:82)).
- **Published per-span values** (all spans of 300 s; for a 1500 s watch the published ones are [1680, 1980), [1980, 2280) and [2280, 2580) s):
  - REG-11, λ = 2.4, seed 1: sessions' hit share 0.000, KV 0.950–0.951, N 29.8–31.0, waiting 169–248, every span `holds` (FILE(docs/decisions.md:2316) to FILE(docs/decisions.md:2318)).
  - REG-12, λ = 2.4, all five burst runs: "every span after the burst is cold (hit share 0.000), full (KV 0.95) and backlogged" (FILE(docs/decisions.md:2480)).
  - REG-14, λ = 2.2, seed 2: hit share 0.000, KV 0.948–0.952, waiting 116–177; all three spans count (FILE(docs/decisions.md:2840) to FILE(docs/decisions.md:2842), FILE(docs/decisions.md:2836)).
  - REG-15, λ = 2.2, seed 12: "Every 300 s window from 1200 s to the end has hit 0.000 and KV 0.947–0.955" (FILE(docs/decisions.md:3105)); **condition 4's levels were computed once before, on another window, the watch's last 1500 s:** KV 0.949, N 30.3 (4.93 × baseline), max N 34 (FILE(docs/decisions.md:3108)).
  - REG-17, λ = 2.0, seed 2: hit 0.000, KV 0.948–0.951 per span; end window KV 0.949, 30.0 running (FILE(docs/decisions.md:3546) to FILE(docs/decisions.md:3548), FILE(docs/decisions.md:3541)).
  - REG-18, λ = 2.0, seeds 4, 3, 5, 6: "In every burst run: hit 0.000 in every span and at the end, KV 0.948–0.952, ≈ 30 running" (FILE(docs/decisions.md:3747)); seeds 3 and 6 each had one span planned below the cold rate (1.623 and 1.760 req/s) with waiting 121 and 101 (FILE(docs/decisions.md:3743), FILE(docs/decisions.md:3745)).
- **What the published spans imply about the exit.** A span `holds` in `gate.burst_backlog` only if no burst request ended in it (FILE(analysis/margin.py:76), FILE(analysis/gate.py:102)). For REG-11 and REG-14 all three published spans hold or count (a span that counts is one that holds, FILE(analysis/gate.py:144)), so no burst request ended at or after 1680 s, unless one never ended or ended with an error status (a span's `done` counts ok ends only, FILE(analysis/margin.py:61)). For REG-12's seeds 2 and 3 the gate's label `pass` needs only one span that holds (FILE(analysis/gate.py:126)), so their exit is not bounded this way; REG-12 published 0 burst requests with a first token in [1980, 2580) s in every seed (FILE(docs/decisions.md:2480)). At most 54 judged spans exist (DERIVED: 10 runs × 4 + 14); 2 of 54 (3.7 %) is the upper end of the range, not an expected share: P(all eleven `loop`) ≈ 0.8 implies about 0.41 % per span if spans fail independently (DERIVED: 1 − 0.8^(1/54)), and 3.7 % per span would make P(all eleven) about 0.13 (DERIVED: 0.963⁵⁴). One run can fail in several spans, so spans are not independent.
- **Batch 2, if it is computed** (P ≈ 0.6 that it is: REG-19 can end without a table; BELIEF, from two lost launches beside six valid runs, DERIVED from FILE(docs/decisions.md:4308) and the three seeds done) **and has at least three stuck runs** (P ≈ 0.7 of that): each run has up to 9 judged spans. The forecast: at 0.41 % per span a stuck run is `loop` with probability about 0.96 (DERIVED: 0.9959⁹), and `not_sustained` in at least two of three stuck runs has probability about 0.004 (DERIVED: 3 × 0.036² × 0.964 + 0.036³). The pessimistic end: at 3.7 % per span, 0.71 per run (DERIVED: 0.963⁹) and about 0.20 for at least two of three (DERIVED: 3 × 0.29² × 0.71 + 0.29³).

That is predicted under both readings of A19 (the trigger's own signals first, or a late first token, alternative 7), so it changes no decision. The run-level reading is predicted to be `differs` for the same reason.

### Decision under each outcome (rule A1), each a ceiling
Each batch is read by these lines on its own, never pooled (N3).
- **a. `loop` in more than half of the stuck runs at a load (n ≥ 3).** A status sentence says at most: "condition 4's registered levels held at the end of the watch, and all four links were present in every 300 s span after the burst's requests had left, in k of n stuck runs at λ = x (both bounds); the order clause is not judged and no loop figure exists; an overload gives the same picture; the loop-cut controls are not run." It also gives:
  - the batch and its standing: batch 1 "thresholds fixed after these runs were reported"; batch 2 "retrospective (by design<; fact (1) | fact (2) | the validity freeze>)", naming "by design" always and each fact that also fails (stopping rule; read (iii) of "What was known"), with decisions.md 2026-11-13 [CORR] "Two reads of REG-19's seed 17" cited; run-time lines and the looks disclosed in the [REG];
  - how many of the k runs have a same-seed control that is `recovered` and holds the four links in no judged span (`reported_counts`, which uses the control's own-baseline flag only, FILE(analysis/c2.py:376); a control whose own baseline was already cold or large can hold the links against the burst run's baseline and still be counted there, rule F round 3, t05; so the flags against the burst run's baseline are given per run beside the count; REG-15's run has no control);
  - at λ = 2.0 only, "batch 2 pending" until batch 2 is computed or reported as not computed; from S (the stopping rule's fact (2)) until then, neither line a's permission to propose D1 and D2 nor line d's 'D1 and D2 not proposed as planned' applies at λ = 2.0 by itself, and wording that relies on either waits for batch 2 or for an entry headed `[DECISION] (owner)` that names the pending batch; a proposal made before S stands, and the batch-2 [RESULT] names it with its commit, with the `done` and `continue` lines REG-19's queue had printed by that commit; once it is reported not computed, "batch 2 not computed: <reason>", with batch 1's standing unchanged (and, for a cause at or after S, with line a's permission withheld as under 'Batches that disagree at λ = 2.0'); once it is computed, both batches' counts side by side, with no summary across them, under the line "Batches that disagree at λ = 2.0".
  - D1 and D2 may then be proposed on the session population as planned, by their own decision.
- **b. λ = 2.4** is given with the words "at the closed-loop warm capacity; three of five controls did not stay healthy (REG-12)" (FILE(docs/decisions.md:2462), FILE(docs/decisions.md:2484)). It is the overload comparison and is not cited as support in C2's status.

If only N < 2 × baseline failed with KV ≥ 0.80: "the running batch was less than twice its baseline", with the baseline given. "The pool was not full", "against C2 for that load" and "D1 and D2 not proposed as planned" need KV < 0.80 in more than half of the stuck runs at the load, with n ≥ 3 (N2). Below that, per run only.
- **e. `not_sustained`:** worded by the link that failed in the span that failed, with the span's planned session rate beside it (`planned`; planned by `t_planned`, the schedule time: in closed loop a planned lull reaches the server later, by the backlog's delay, FILE(analysis/load.py:25)). "Re-warmed" only if the reuse link failed. If only the uncached rate failed: "the recomputed work fell below twice its baseline in k spans", with the span's reuse and completion rate beside it. If only N or KV failed: "the batch (or the pool) was below its level in span …, with the reuse still lost". If it is the label of more than half of the stuck runs at a load (n ≥ 3), the confirmation run's registration must read every span, not only the end window; a retrospective batch 2 that meets this line carries the same duty (rule F round 10, BG-O6).

Both counts are then given side by side with each batch's standing and with each batch's number of judged spans and of judged spans that fail a link (rule F round 11, BK-O6: a batch-2 run has up to 9 judged spans and most batch-1 runs up to 4, so the span count alone can make the batches disagree, alternative 5; DERIVED there: at 3.7 % per span a run is `loop` with probability 0.86 at 4 spans and 0.71 at 9, 0.963⁴ and 0.963⁹), and C2's status for λ = 2.0 names the line each batch met (or "none") and claims neither. When the batches disagree, neither line a's permission to propose D1 and D2 nor line d's "D1 and D2 not proposed as planned" applies by itself; any wording that relies on either waits for an entry headed `[DECISION] (owner)` that cites both batches; a delegate entry does not release either line (rule F round 12, CG3, cross-applied by the owner-proxy on draft 18, CL4). A file `final.sh` saved never makes REG-19 'end without the table that `final.sh` saves'. ### Reported, never judged
- **Per run:** the baseline; the levels with what failed; every span of the watch with its four values, the links that failed, whether it was judged, and its planned session rate (`c2.planned_rates`, through `gate.planned_session_rate`); the exit; the row counts (`c2.row_counts`).
- **The same-seed control** (`c2.control_readout`): its registered verdict and its links over the burst run's judged spans, against its own baseline and against the burst run's baseline. A control that is a **single same-seed control** is labelled so wherever it is quoted. A queue that the load alone explains would show the links in the control too, if the control's own baseline was warm; a control already cold or large in [300, 900) s cannot double its own baseline, which is why the second comparison is given (rule F round 2, trace t08). With no judged span the readout's flags are missing, not False. REG-15's run has no control. It carries no label.
- **Onsets** (`c2.onsets`): the first 10 s grid time after the burst's start at which the trailing 60 s crosses: KV ≥ 0.9; N ≥ 2 × baseline; reuse ≤ baseline − 0.06 with at least 20 turns; session uncached rate ≥ 2 × baseline. Equal times are reported as one group.
- **Onset reading** (`c2.onset_reading`). The crossing lags differ by construction: for a step at one instant from the baseline value to the end-window value, a trailing 60 s mean crosses the level 60 × (level − before) ÷ (after − before) seconds after the step. At values on record that is about 3.6 s for the reuse (DERIVED: 60 × 0.06 / 1.0; 4.3 s on a baseline of 0.84), 11.5 to 17 s for the uncached rate (DERIVED: 60 / (6.2 − 1) to 60 / (4.5 − 1)), 15 s for N (60 × 6 / 24) and about 56 s for KV (DERIVED: 60 × (0.9 − 0.24) / (0.95 − 0.24), warm KV 0.23–0.24 from FILE(docs/decisions.md:2477) and FILE(docs/decisions.md:2478)). The code takes each run's own baseline and end-window values, so each onset minus its own lag is the step time it implies. For each pair in the plan's order (reuse, uncached rate, N, KV), `plan` if the later signal's implied step is more than one grid step (10 s) after the earlier one's, `reversed` if more than 10 s before, `together` otherwise. The run's reading: `incomplete` if a signal has no onset or its end value does not pass its level; `differs` if any pair is `reversed`; `plan_order_beyond_lags` if every pair is `plan`; else `not_distinguishable_from_simultaneous`. The grid step is in the tolerance because onsets are rounded up to the 10 s grid: without it, four signals stepping together read as ordered in 2 of 10 step phases (rule F round 2, trace t05 O). A ramp crosses with another lag; that is not modelled.
- **The eviction link read directly** (`c2.eviction_readout`): the engine samples 1 % of its KV blocks and, when a sampled block is taken for a new allocation, records the time since its last access (`vllm:kv_block_idle_before_evict_seconds`; SOURCE(vLLM 0.32.0 vllm/v1/core/kv_cache_metrics.py:KVCacheMetricsCollector.on_block_evicted); SOURCE(vLLM 0.32.0 vllm/v1/core/block_pool.py:_maybe_evict_cached_block)). For the baseline and for the stretch after the exit (after the burst's end where there is no exit): what the histogram gained, the bucket holding the median with its lower and upper edge, the shares at or below 5 s and 30 s, and the median time between the first tokens of a session's consecutive turns (`c2.turn_spacing`). A bucket that is lower than at the scrape before, at any scrape of the window, flags the window `reset`, and it is not read (N8). A restart behind a scrape that has values but none of this histogram's keys is not flagged (rule F round 3, t06 b); whether `metrics.jsonl` has such scrapes is not checked here. Where the turn spacing falls inside the median's bucket, the two are reported as not separable.
  - **Prediction (DERIVED in FILE(agent/theory/k1_held_prefix.md:21) and FILE(agent/theory/k1_held_prefix.md:22), not reviewed; BELIEF as a forecast):** warm, an idle prefix is overwritten about 64 s after its release, so the median falls in the (60, 120] s bucket, far above a turn spacing of about 7 s; in the cold state about 1 s after its release, so the median is the time a request holds its blocks plus that, in the (10, 20] or (20, 30] s bucket, and below the turn spacing there.
  - **If it is wrong:** a cold-state median above the turn spacing would mean prefixes outlive the gap and are still not reused, which the loop does not explain; a warm median below the turn spacing would contradict the warm counter hit rate of about 0.84 (FILE(docs/decisions.md:3747)). Either is reported as against the loop's eviction link.

### Alternatives to state with any result
1. **Overload, not a loop.** At λ = 2.4 the closed-loop warm capacity is reached (FILE(docs/claims.md:45)), and REG-12's seed-5 control fell into the same cold, full, backlogged state with no burst (FILE(docs/decisions.md:2478)). There `loop` holds with no history dependence. The control readout shows it per run; PROTOCOL §3 conditions 2, 5 and 6 decide it.
2. **The label follows from the selection.** The verdict `stuck` already requires a low hit rate at the end; the levels then nearly follow. What is not selected on is the spans before the end window.
3. **The preemption cycle of Ao et al.** A full pool with a large batch is also what their limit cycle shows. **This registration does not separate it.** The registered comparison (preemptions per minute against the same seed's control, decisions.md 2026-11-01) has no code and no registration (FILE(docs/definitions.md:102)).
4. **A schedule lull.** A span planned below the cold rate can shrink the batch and KV with the cache still lost; each span's planned rate is reported, and `not_sustained` is worded by the link that failed (line e). The planned rate is by `t_planned`, the schedule time; in closed loop a lull reaches the server later, by the backlog's delay.
5. **More spans, more chances.** A run with 14 judged spans is likelier to be `not_sustained` than one with 4; the number of judged spans is reported per run and no rate is compared across watch lengths.
6. **The deepest backlogs drop out.** The longest burst tails leave the fewest judged spans, so the most stuck runs are the likeliest to be `undefined`; the spans that exist are reported for those runs.
7. **Late first tokens, for any onset result.** Session signals are read by first token, and the uncached rate is session work per second. While the burst shares the server, session turns are served late or not at all and the uncached rate is diluted, so both cross late for reasons of measurement (FILE(docs/drafts/reviews-2026-11-13/rulef-reg22-draft5-r3.md): t03b F; t03 C and C2, where a cache lost at 900 s and one lost at 1000 s give the same onsets and reading). A `reversed` pair says nothing about when the cache was lost unless every trailing 60 s window through the burst held at least 20 later turns, which this registration does not compute. The reuse is a ratio and is not diluted while such a window holds 20 turns; only the pairs with the uncached rate carry the dilution.

### Order with REG-21 (both directions)
- **a.** Neither REG-21's nor REG-22's batch 1 is computed until both registrations are committed with their [DECISION] (delegate) entries. After that the order of the two computations is free. A change to one of REG-22's frozen files after this entry and before its batch 1 is reported, and batch 1 is then values without labels, or waits for the owner (as under (c)).
- **b.** If REG-21 is not registered when REG-22 is ready, REG-22's batch 1 waits. The one exception: a [DECISION] (delegate) records that REG-21 is deferred and names the commit at which REG-21's thresholds, label map and judged functions stand. A change to them after REG-22's batch-1 table exists is a threshold chosen after its data (rule A5, not delegated); REG-21's batch 1 is then reported as values without labels, or waits for the owner. ("After a batch-1 table exists", here and in (c), is tested so: a batch's first run is the first printed or displayed output, by any entry point (the batch's command, `python -c`, a REPL, another module), of that batch's table (`c2.reg22_table`, or under (c) `k3w.reg21_table`) on real run folders, or of a label or judged value it gives for one of that batch's runs (for REG-22, a result of `c2.levels`, `c2.links`, `c2.sustain` or `c2.condition4`); the registration that owns the batch states in its entry that none was printed before its entry commit, or gives the time of the first; a change counts as made before the table exists only if its commit is a strict ancestor of the first commit that adds the saved output of that batch's first run (the stopping rule's third bullet) and its committer time is earlier than the UTC start time in that file's name, compared as instants. That output is committed at once and alone; one committed late or with other changes still counts, the breach is reported, and every other change in that commit counts as after. If that first run did not write its file as the third bullet says, the batch's table counts as existing from the earliest of the time of that first output where it is known, the entry commit of the registration that owns the batch and, under (b), the commit the deferral [DECISION] names: no change made after that commit counts as made before the table exists, and a later saved run does not take its place.) REG-21's draft gains REG-22's table under "What was known". REG-22's batch 2 waits until REG-21 is registered, unless the same [DECISION] states that REG-21's batch 2 is no longer read blind. That [DECISION] states which of the two it takes, and if it takes the second, the consequence for REG-21's batch 2 in the same entry.
- **c.** If REG-21's batch 1 is computed before REG-22's entries are committed, REG-22's "What was known" gains REG-21's table, and REG-22's constants, label map and judged functions must be those of `727d1f2`. A change to them after that table exists is a threshold chosen after its data (rule A5, not delegated): batch 1 is then reported as values without labels, or waits for the owner. Batch 2 keeps its labels if the freeze below holds.

### Stopping rule
- **Batch 1** is computed once, after order (a) or (b) above holds: `uv run python -m analysis.c2 reg22`.
- **Batch 2** is computed once, after REG-19's final [RESULT] and the comparison under "Runs": `uv run python -m analysis.c2 reg22 2`. REG-20's gate (`uv run python -m analysis.k1 reg20_a_may_start`), whose inputs batch 2 prints, is computed before it, or both results state the order. In the same command line as batch 2's command, and before it, fact (1)'s two commands and the two checks printed beside them, `git rev-parse HEAD` (this is B), `uv run python -V`, `uv --version`, `uv run python -c 'import analysis, numpy; print(analysis.__file__, numpy.__version__)'` (so that a shadowed `analysis` or an unsynced venv shows) and an unrestricted `git status --porcelain` are run and their output is written at the top of the batch file (rule F round 10, BG-O1 and BG-O2; rule F round 11, BK-O1 and BK-O4; a reporting duty: a breach is reported and changes neither fact).
- Both run from committed code: the command refuses when `analysis/` or `tests/` holds a modified or untracked file; `uv run pytest` and `python3 tools/check_docs.py` pass before. **Each batch's output is saved verbatim in `docs/probe/reg22/batch<k>_<YYYYMMDDTHHMMSSZ>.txt`, whose name carries the UTC time at which the command was started, committed at once and alone** (the time taken with `date -u` in the same command line that runs the batch and redirects its stdout to that file, a line the [RESULT] quotes; REG-21 reads the time of REG-22's batch 1 from it; a batch whose first run did not write its file this way is a deviation, reported, and changes none of REG-22's labels; for the order rules, see order (b); a batch file whose stamp is later than its commit's committer time counts as a first run that did not write its file this way); the [RESULT] quotes from it and gives its path, sha256 and commit. A second run of a batch's command is a deviation and is logged.
- **The judged path** (described for the reader; the freeze below covers whole files) is everything `reg22_table` runs before the readouts, and everything those call, transitively, with the module constants they read: in `analysis/c2.py` the constants `C2` and `REG22`, `windows`, `gauge`, `reuse_in`, `session_uncached_rate`, `baseline`, `levels`, `last_burst_end`, `links`, `sustain`, `condition4`'s label, `batch_runs`, `reg22_table`; and `k1.later_turns`, `margin.is_burst_request`, `load._covered`, `load.verdict`, `load._level`, `load.find_runs`, `load.load_run`, `load._jsonl`, `load.metrics_wide`, `load.RUNS`, `stats.cp_upper`, `k3w.batch2_runs` with the keys of `k3w.REG21` it reads, and `withheld.lifted`, `keep`, `sealed_by`, `guard`, `unsealed_ids`, `SEALS`, `DECISIONS` (N4).
- **This text, written under the review-stop rule's item 4, keeps the freeze, the two facts, the validity cut and the not-computed rules, which decide whether batch 2 is computed and with which words; items of its review are applied as usual, and no further stop exists** (rule F round 11's addendum, BK-S4; decisions.md 2026-11-13 [DECISION] (delegate), round 3's stop, item 5, FILE(docs/decisions.md:4553)). **So from this entry to batch 2 the frozen files do not change, with no exception** (the judged path and the readouts that lines a, e and h quote, `onsets`, `onset_reading`, `planned_rates`, `control_readout`, `reported_counts` and the `__main__` block, all lie in them). The frozen files are every file the batch command imports, by the import closure of `analysis/c2.py` at this entry's commit (function-level imports included; computed with Python's `ast`), and the three files that fix the environment: `analysis/__init__.py`, `analysis/c2.py`, `analysis/derived.py`, `analysis/floor.py`, `analysis/gate.py`, `analysis/k1.py`, `analysis/k3.py`, `analysis/k3w.py`, `analysis/load.py`, `analysis/margin.py`, `analysis/modelf.py`, `analysis/modelf_sim.py`, `analysis/stats.py`, `analysis/tables.py`, `analysis/withheld.py`, `harness/__init__.py`, `harness/checks.py`, `harness/config.py`, `harness/env_snapshot.py`, `harness/loadgen.py`, `harness/recorder.py`, `harness/run.py`, `harness/trigger.py`, `harness/workload.py`, `pyproject.toml`, `uv.lock`, `.python-version` (27 files; `harness/run.py` imports `env_snapshot`, `trigger` and `loadgen` at its top, FILE(harness/run.py:23), and `gate.py` and `k3.py` import `harness.run` inside functions). If the closure computed at E differs from this list, the union is frozen and the [DECISION] (delegate) prints both. The closure at E is computed by a committed script that counts `from <package> import <name>` as an import of `<package>/<name>.py` where that file exists; its output is saved with the [DECISION] (delegate), and fact (1)'s commands name the union (rule F round 10, BG2). The judged path lies inside them; whether a change touches it is not asked, so no hunk is ever argued to lie outside it. A new seal would be a change too; every pending registration's seal is already in `withheld.SEALS` (FILE(analysis/withheld.py:26)), REG-20's arms A and B included (its pattern `*_l1pl350ol_r2.[05]_w3000_s1[5-9]` covers λ = 2.0 and 2.5, FILE(analysis/withheld.py:28)), so no seal needs adding whenever arm B runs (rule F round 10, BG-O5), and any change to these files waits until both REG-21's and REG-22's batch 2 are computed or declared not computed; REG-20's work and every other new code go into new files until then. **Batch 2 is labelled retrospective by design (read (iii), "What was known"); it would have been primary only if two facts in git held,** both shown in the batch-2 [RESULT] as the verbatim output of their commands. Let E be the later of the two commits that append this [REG] and its [DECISION] (delegate), and B the commit batch 2 runs from: the tip of `main` when its command starts, checked out in the main working tree, whose `runs/` is the one `load.RUNS` names (FILE(analysis/load.py:11)). (1) **No commit touches a frozen file:** `git log --full-history --format='%H %ct %s' E..B -- <the frozen files>` prints nothing (without `--full-history`, git's default history simplification hides a change and its revert made on a side branch that was merged, which this fact counts), and `git status --porcelain -- <the frozen files>` prints nothing in that checkout. Beside them two checks on the log are printed: `git merge-base --is-ancestor E B && echo ancestor || echo not_ancestor` (B descends from E) and `git diff --stat E B -- <the frozen files>` (the net change) (rule F round 11, BK-O1). Any change counts, whatever it touches and however small, and a later commit that reverts it does not undo it. (2) **This entry precedes REG-19's table:** a REG-19 table file is a file named `reg19_final_<stamp>.txt` or `reg19_final_err_<stamp>.txt` whose `<stamp>` begins with a UTC time `YYYYMMDDTHHMMSSZ` (the names `final.sh` writes, FILE(docs/probe/20261113_reg19/ops_r3/final.sh:20), FILE(docs/probe/20261113_reg19/ops_r3/common.sh:42)); other names matching `reg19_final_*`, such as the review bundles' `reg19_final_sh_for_reference.sh` (committed since `ab6988f`), are not table files and are listed as such. Let S be the earliest such UTC time among the table files anywhere in the repository's working tree (`find . -name 'reg19_final_*' -not -path './.git/*' | grep -E '/reg19_final_(err_)?[0-9]{8}T[0-9]{6}Z[^/]*$'`; the same `find` piped to `grep -vE` with that expression lists the other names), every table file that any commit on any ref adds (`git log -m --all --reflog --full-history --no-renames --diff-filter=A --name-only --format='%H %ct' -- ':(glob)**/reg19_final_*' | awk '/^[0-9a-f]+ [0-9]+$/ {c=$0; next} NF {print c, $0}' | grep -E ' (.*/)?reg19_final_(err_)?[0-9]{8}T[0-9]{6}Z[^/]*$'`, one line per added table file with its commit and committer time; `--no-renames` so that a file renamed to a table-file name counts as added; `--reflog` so that an older stash entry, or a commit that only a reflog still reaches, counts too: in a throwaway repository with two stash entries that each add a table file, `--all` printed only the newer one's and `--reflog` both, DERIVED by the agent in a scratch repository; rule F round 11, BK-O2), and every such time a decisions.md entry quotes for a table file (`grep -noE 'reg19_final_(err_)?[0-9]{8}T[0-9]{6}Z' docs/decisions.md`). Two stamps that this grep prints are synthetic and do not count toward S: 20261114T010203Z and 20261114T020000Z. Rule F round 11's BK2 trace (step 8) wrote them for files in a throwaway repository (FILE(docs/drafts/reviews-2026-11-13/rulef-reg22-draft16-r11.md:74)), and this [REG] quotes that review verbatim. They are fixed here, before any table file exists. The [RESULT] lists the grep's lines for them as synthetic. A file with either stamp in a working tree, or added by a commit, still counts (rule F round 12, CG1). The `find` is run in every working tree that `git worktree list` names, and the whole output of the three commands goes into the batch-2 [RESULT]; a name that matches `^reg19_final_(err_)?[0-9]{8}T[0-9]{6}Z` without ending in `.txt` is a table file too, so that the set is REG-21's (its fact (2)) and the review-stop rule's (FILE(docs/decisions.md:4437), whose check uses these three commands without `--reflog`, so that this fact's `git log` can only find more, FILE(docs/decisions.md:4555)) (REG-21's owner-proxy, BF1 and BF3; stricter). Fact (2) holds if E's committer time (`git log -1 --format=%ct E`) is earlier than S, compared as instants (this Mac commits at +0600, so local clock readings are never compared; the same second counts as after), and no commit that adds a table file is E or an ancestor of E (`git merge-base --is-ancestor <commit> E && echo ancestor || echo not_ancestor`, BG-O1). Everywhere else in this entry ("Runs", the duties, the limits, the validity freeze), "a `reg19_final_*` file" and "every file named `reg19_final_*`" read "a REG-19 table file" and "every REG-19 table file". `final.sh` takes its stamp before it computes the table (FILE(docs/probe/20261113_reg19/ops_r3/final.sh:20), FILE(docs/probe/20261113_reg19/ops_r3/final.sh:29)), so S is no later than the first moment REG-19's table could be seen. **Duties, each a breach reported in the batch-2 [RESULT] if missed, none of which changes (2):** every REG-19 table file is committed on `main`, alone, in the first commit after it is written; a pair set aside after a failed run is committed where it was set aside, and the [OPS] entry that `final.sh` requires for a second try quotes the set-aside files' names; before batch 2's command runs, every such file in the working tree is committed; no decisions.md entry, saved review or other committed text writes a table-file name with a stamp that `final.sh` did not write, apart from the two synthetic names that rule F round 11's saved review holds (FILE(docs/drafts/reviews-2026-11-13/rulef-reg22-draft16-r11.md:74)), its review-bundle copies and this [REG]'s verbatim quote of it; a decisions.md entry that does so still counts toward S as it stands, except the two synthetic stamps named above; a saved review or other committed text is not searched and does not count toward S (rule F round 10, BG-O8; rule F round 12, CG1). Batch 2 is labelled retrospective whether or not the facts hold, and each fact that fails is named: wherever a batch's standing is given (line a, "Batches that disagree at λ = 2.0") it reads "retrospective (by design<; fact (1) | fact (2) | the validity freeze>)", naming "by design" always and each fact that also fails; it enters that line's disagreement test as a computed batch, so it can withhold line a's permission and line d's wording, and no sentence rests on it alone; but if fact (1) fails through a commit whose committer time is at or after S, or through a line of `git status`, a fix under the fix clause included, batch 2 is reported per run with its labels and counts in 'Batches that disagree at λ = 2.0' as a batch that met none of the lines, until an entry headed `[DECISION] (owner)` names that change (rule F round 12, CG2); no review, statement, [CORR] or later commit restores primary standing; only the owner can, by an entry made before batch 1 is computed (the plan the owner approved, FILE(docs/drafts/plan_2026-11-13.md:54), FILE(docs/decisions.md:4337)). That entry is headed `[DECISION] (owner)`; a delegate entry restores nothing (rule F round 12, CG3, applied by the agent to CH4's sentence, as REG-21's draft 27 does). Apart from read (iii), the label follows from these facts alone: if the [RESULT] leaves one out or quotes one wrongly, a [CORR] corrects the quote and the label is the one the facts give. **Limits, stated before the data:** a REG-19 table file moved out of the repository and never committed or quoted, a hand run of REG-19's table that saves nothing, and a local history rewritten after the fact cannot be detected; only a copy pushed elsewhere would witness the history (pushing `main` is the owner's choice). No REG-19 table file is deleted or moved out of the repository, and no commit from E to batch 2 is amended, rebased or given a committer date by hand. **Validity and the run set are frozen from E too:** batch 2 is also retrospective (as above) if, after E and before S, the validity flag of a run matching the batch-2 pattern is set or changed other than by the harness's checks at the run's end or the queue's recheck under the checks pinned for REG-19 (`CHECKS_COMMIT`, FILE(docs/probe/20261113_reg19/ops_r3/common.sh:30)), or a valid burst run of a REG-19 seed is rerun; a rerun of a lost or invalid run under REG-19's registered rules is not such a change. A change at or after S ends batch 2 ("Runs", not computed), which takes precedence, with the consequence that 'Batches that disagree at λ = 2.0' gives it. Lines a, d, e and h, the line "Batches that disagree at λ = 2.0" and batch 1's [RESULT] quote the frozen output with the [CORR] named; if any label differs between the two, batch 2 is reported per run with both labels and counts in 'Batches that disagree at λ = 2.0' as a batch that met none of the lines until an entry headed `[DECISION] (owner)`; a delegate entry does not release any of these lines (rule F round 12, CG3). A defect found after batch 2 is computed is handled the same way, and the frozen labels are the ones quoted. The batch-2 [RESULT] lists every commit from E to B on the frozen files (there should be none).

> ## 3. The reading of PROTOCOL's order clause
>
> - **Weaker or stronger.** `sustain` is stronger than the end-window levels in duration and weaker than an order test in kind. It tests that the levels co-occur in every 300 s span; it tests no direction. At 300 s resolution it misses a full recovery of up to 69 s [t10].
> - **Pure overload.** Yes, it gets `loop` [t06 A, C]. Nothing in the label uses the control, the warm capacity or the schedule.
> - **Does the registration name it.** Yes, in Alternatives 2, for λ = 2.4 only. It does not compute the cheap separators that exist: the same-seed control's links at the same absolute spans, and the control's verdict per judged run.
> - **The premise is untagged.** "On a burst run the first events are the trigger's … and the hit rate falls after them" carries no evidence tag, and the registration says nobody computed the onsets. The only evidence it will produce on this is the readout of trace J, which is biased towards the plan's order.
>
> ## 4. "What was known" and the prediction
>
> "Not computed by anyone … it cannot be checked from a file" is wrong on both counts. Registered functions already run on these runs compute:
> - **Per-span KV, N, cached share, cold flag and burst completions** for [1680, 1980), [1980, 2280) and [2280, 2580), which are three of REG-22's five grid spans: FILE(analysis/margin.py:66–79) through FILE(analysis/gate.py:91–103, 139, 400), used by the gates of REG-11, 12, 14, 17 and 18. If the exit falls in (1380, 1680], these are exactly the judged spans [t02 S2].
> - **For REG-15:** `watch_broken` on REG-22's exact grid, a 300 s timeline of KV and N, and the span test over the watch (FILE(analysis/gate.py:949–964, 989–1008)).
> - **Burst first tokens in the end window** (FILE(analysis/gate.py:479–494)), which decides the "fewer than two spans" case.
> - **The KV onset**, same 60 s window and same 0.9 level (FILE(analysis/gate.py:1361–1370, 1386)).
>
> Whether those values were printed in the [RESULT] entries I may not read. What is new is the uncached rate, reuse in the first two spans, the exact exit, three of the four onsets and the histograms.
>
> Other gaps:
> - The description of REG-21 omits that its command also prints the uncached rate and reuse per 300 s span on the same grid (FILE(analysis/k3w.py:403–434, 467)): REG-22's first two links.
> - "10–12 runs have the verdict stuck" forecasts a reported fact. The brief for this review says two of the 13 are `bad_baseline`; if so, 12 is impossible.
> - P ≈ 0.95 for the levels is understated: KV 0.95 at the end is reported for every run, and N follows from KV. `not_memory_limited` is close to excluded for batch 1 before computing.
> - The batch-2 forecast (at least four fifths `loop`) ignores exposure. Batch-1 runs have at most 4 judged spans, batch 2 has 9, REG-15 has 14 [t02 S4]. "0–2 `not_sustained`" in batch 1 implies up to about 5 % per span, which gives P(no failing span in 9) = 0.63. The two forecasts agree only below about 2.4 % per span. REG-15's run, the most exposed, is not listed as a candidate.
>
> ## 5. Strongest alternative for each label
>
> - **`loop`:** a queue persists in a pool that holds 30 requests, and everything else follows mechanically: a queue fills the pool, a full pool evicts prefixes. Overload, a slowly draining queue or a slower GPU give the same picture. Separators: the control at the same spans, the load against the warm capacity, GPU clock per span (`gate.span_clock`), conditions 5–6, the loop-cut controls. Also selection: `stuck` already requires a low hit rate at the end.
> - **`not_memory_limited`:** a high baseline N near capacity (trace G), or a lull in the last 600 s. Separator: which of the three levels failed, and per-span values.
> - **`not_sustained`:** a schedule lull in one span (separator: planned session rate per span next to the links), a throughput dip with a cold cache (trace F), or more spans giving more chances to fail.
> - **`undefined`:** the deepest backlogs have the longest burst tails, so the most stuck runs are the likeliest to drop out of k of n. Separator: report the links for the spans that exist, and the burst rows by status.

> ## 3. Traces and findings on the code
>
> ### Judged rules
>
> - **(a) One failing span decides.**
>   - A span cannot "fail" because of an unreadable value. Any missing value, the baseline's included, makes `links` return None (c2.py:118–119), never False. With an unreadable baseline every span is None and the run is `undefined` [t01 (iv)].
>   - The only partial inputs left are rows without `cached_tokens` and requests that got a first token but never finished. Both push the two cache links towards holding, not failing.
>   - **I could not break (a).**
> - **The code diff changes labels only as announced.** I compared labels on 960 synthetic runs. The grid crossed the cache state, KV, scrape holes, the exit time, and thinning to 19 later turns. The labels differ in 62 runs [t02 §1], every one explained:
>   - 18 runs go from `undefined` to `not_sustained`: a judged span fails while another has a missing value (O2).
>   - 44 runs go from `loop` or `not_sustained` to `undefined`: fewer than 20 later turns (O4).
> - **(b) The minimum of 20 later turns.**
>   - These runs are nowhere near it (DERIVED from the configs: 8 turns, session rate λ/8, cold completion 1.73 req/s). The baseline [300, 900) holds about 1050–1260 later turns. A cold 300 s span holds at least about 430. A 60 s onset window holds at least about 86.
>   - A span falls under 20 only if the server nearly stops. That span is then None, so the run is `undefined` rather than `not_sustained`, even though its uncached rate (about 0) would fail link 2. This is consistent with case 5 and not plausible on valid runs (BELIEF).
> - **(c) Unjudged spans now computed.** They cannot change a label.
>   - A scrape hole, no later turn, or a cache back inside the unjudged span all leave the label at `loop` [t02 §3].
>   - `links_failed` collects judged spans only (c2.py:147).
>   - The only raise inside `links` is `session_uncached_rate`'s check over the whole run (c2.py:72), and `baseline` makes it first, both before and after the change.
>
> ### Reported-only code
>
> - **The readouts cannot change or delay a label.**
>   - `condition4(..., with_readouts=False)` calls none of the four readouts and does not call `find_runs` [t04 §1].
>   - `reg22_table` computes every label and the counts before the first readout [t04 §2].
>   - Each row's label is recomputed in a second pass (c2.py:345), after the earlier runs' readouts have run. It equals the first pass because no real readout changes its inputs (read through: `later_turns` copies; `control_readout` reads `su` only).
>   - A readout that did change what it is handed would alter the printed `sustain` beside an unchanged label [t04 §2] (optional item 4).
> - **`control_readout` name mapping** [t03]:
>   - All 17 burst configs map to an existing control with the same seed, rate, duration, sessions, steps, server arguments, windows, and `control_t_s` = 1080. That covers REG-11 (explicit entry, c2.py:304; the glob does not match the `_s2` controls or the open-loop control) and REG-19's five `w3000` seeds.
>   - REG-15's `confirm_…` config gives "this config has no control", which matches line 73. The only 2.2 controls are REG-14's `_s2` and REG-16's `long_s14`.
>   - Two valid controls give "2 valid runs of …"; none gives "0 valid runs of …" [t04 §3].
>   - The real `load.verdict` runs on a control (control_t_s 1080, verdict baseline [480, 1080)) [t06 V]. The links are taken over the burst run's window [300, 900), on the control's own data.
> - **Sealed controls.** A sealed control cannot arise in either batch.
>   - REG-19's seal pattern `*_l1pl350cl_r2.0_w3000_s1[5-9]` covers burst runs and controls alike. The heading that lets batch 2 run lifts both [t04 §4].
>   - No batch-1 control is sealed.
>   - If one were sealed, the readout would say "0 valid runs", the same as absent or invalid; only stderr names the seal.
> - **The control readout can point the wrong way** [t08 §1]. Line 73 says "a queue that the load alone explains would show the links in the control too". That holds only if the control's [300, 900) was warm.
>   - Synthetic control in the same cold, full state by the load alone, tipping at 1200, 950, 850 or 700 s: `links_hold_in_every_span` True.
>   - The same control tipping at 500 or 200 s: False. Its own baseline is already cold or large, so u and N cannot double.
>   - Against the burst run's baseline, its links hold in every case.
>   - **Likelihood: low for judged runs (BELIEF).** The burst twin had a good baseline on the same schedule. Optional item 2.
> - **No-exit runs.** A burst run with no exit gives the control readout no spans and `links_hold_in_every_span` False rather than None [t08 §3].
> - **`row_counts` is right** [t04 §5]: 7 rows without `cached_tokens` and 3 unfinished with a first token give 7 and 3; requests that never started are not counted.
> - **The `reset` flag does not do what line 75 says.** It compares only the first and last scrape (c2.py:239–242). A restart after which every bucket climbs past its start is not flagged: the count printed is 800 where 1000 + 1300 were gained, and the median and shares come from two unrelated counters [t05 H]. See N8.
> - **The lower bound is right.** 1 − cp_upper(n − k, n) equals the one-sided 95 % Clopper–Pearson lower bound to within 5e-16 for n ≤ 14 [t04 §6]. Examples: 3 of 3 gives 0.368; 4 of 5 gives 0.343; 2 of 2 gives 0.224.
> - **The clean-tree check is right.** `_dirty` (c2.py:359–361) runs before `reg22_table`. It would refuse to run on the current working tree.

> ## 4. Strongest alternative explanation, and whether the analysis can change a decision
>
> **For any `loop` count:** a queue that the load alone sustains gives the same four links. The pool holds about 30 requests, and a full pool evicts prefixes (D16:9). Only PROTOCOL §3's conditions 2, 5 and 6 and the loop-cut controls separate the two. The draft says so.
>
> **For a disagreement between batches:** batch 1 runs have up to 4 judged spans each (D16:84, 54 spans over 11 runs), and batch 2 runs up to 9 (D16:85). `not_sustained` needs one failing span, so at the same per-span rate a batch-2 run is less often `loop`. At the pessimistic 3.7 % per span, a run is `loop` with probability 0.86 at 4 spans and 0.71 at 9 (DERIVED: 0.963⁴, 0.963⁹). So a disagreement can come from span count alone (BK-O6).
>
> **Can it change a decision?** Yes, at λ = 2.0, through line a (D1/D2 permission), line d, line e's duty and the disagreement test: P ≈ 0.05 for batch 1 (BELIEF) and ≈ 0.002–0.084 for batch 2 (DERIVED, D16:11).
> - Under the stop, batch 2 still enters the disagreement test as a computed batch (BC1), so that probability is unchanged. What the stop removes is any sentence resting on batch 2 alone, and with it the only reading of condition 4 registered before its data. That cost is to the paper's claim C2, not only to its words. I disagree here with "that would cost little" (FILE(docs/drafts/reviews-2026-11-13/proxy-reg22-draft15-delta.md), notes for the owner).
> - BK3 adds a window, from S to batch 2, in which neither line a nor line d applies by itself.
>

Round 3's owner-proxy approved the content of both for REG-22, with its note on "the same definition" (They differ in form and are the same set only because `final.sh` writes only `.txt` names.). Rule F round 11 reviewed both in its section 5, quoted here verbatim:

> ## 5. The two review-stop entries (delegate decisions)
>
> **BK-S1. When the further entry is committed.** The amendment applies items against either entry "by a further entry before any batch is computed" (FILE(docs/decisions.md:4437), its "order" item). The rule decides what REG-22's text becomes, so it must be settled before E.
> - Replacement: "before E of either registration, and REG-21's and REG-22's entries cite it".
> - Class: a stricter rule. Owner-proxy pass: yes.
>
> **BK-S2. Part (2) and REG-22's owner-proxy disagree, and neither entry says which holds.**
> - REG-22's owner-proxy classed a whole kind of change in advance: "A pass for any change to fact (1), fact (2) or the validity freeze beyond BH1, BH2 and BH9. Under the review-stop entry such a change is not wording, so it brings the stop" (FILE(docs/drafts/reviews-2026-11-13/proxy-reg22-draft15-delta.md:160)).
> - Draft 16 makes such changes, and its change log says so: the BF1/BF3 sentence and BG3 (D16:218, D16:221).
> - Part (2) makes "the class its reviewer states" govern. These changes' reviewers (REG-21's proxy; rule F round 10) classed them as stricter or wording. The amendment applied its rule to round 2 without naming line 160.
> - If line 160 governs, round 2 already stopped. The outcome is the same as this round's, but the record must say which reading was used.
> - Add to part (2): "Where two reviewers of the same registration class one change differently, or one classes a kind of change in advance, the class that is none of wording, a tag, a stricter rule or a reporting duty holds; applied to round 2, REG-22's owner-proxy's line 160 makes draft 16's changes to fact (2) and the validity freeze beyond BH1, BH2 and BH9 a stop from round 2, with the same effect as round 3's."
> - Class: a stricter rule and a disclosure. Owner-proxy pass: yes.
>
> **BK-S3. Who states whether an item is "about batch 2's standing"?** Item 3 lists the scope, and part (2) settles the class, not the standing.
> - Add: "Whether an item is about batch 2's standing is stated by its reviewer; where none states it, the owner-proxy of the same round states it; an item no one has stated counts as about batch 2's standing."
> - Class: a stricter rule.
>
> **BK-S4. What the text after the stop keeps.** Item 4 gives that text "its own rule F review and owner-proxy pass" but does not say what it keeps.
> - Under BC1 a retrospective batch 2 is still computed and still withholds lines, so the freeze, facts (1) and (2) (with BK2's commands), the validity cut at S and BG4 still decide whether it is computed and under which cause words.
> - Add: "The text written under item 4 keeps the freeze, the two facts, the validity cut and the not-computed rules, which decide whether batch 2 is computed and with which words; items of its review are applied as usual, and no further stop exists."
> - Class: a stricter rule.
>
> **BK-S5. "Selects on no data" needs a qualifier.** The entry is free of run data. But part (2) was adopted after round 2's items were known and was then used to class them (FILE(docs/decisions.md:4437)): a rule chosen after seeing what it judges (rule A5, in kind).
> - Add to the amendment: "Part (2) was adopted after round 2's items and their reviewers' classes were known, and applied to them."
> - Class: a disclosure.
>
> **BK-S6. Item 5's check has no command.** "The entry is committed before the first commit that adds a `reg19_final_*` file", read by part (1), names no command.
> - Name BK2's three commands there, with `--no-renames`.
> - Class: a stricter rule.

- **The stop entry** (FILE(docs/decisions.md:4541)) was committed as a delegate decision before its own rule F review and owner-proxy pass. Round 4's owner-proxy approved its content for REG-22. Rule F round 12 reviewed it; its words, verbatim:

> **BK-S1–S6 in the stop entry (decisions.md:4548–4555):** applied substantively. Two notes:
> - (a) Item 2 adds BI-S1's definition ("its consequence is batch 2's label"). This is narrower than review-stop item 3's "what a retrospective batch 2 does", and BK-S4's own claim to concern batch 2's standing rests on item 3. It is harmless now that no further stop exists.
> - (b) BK-S6's commands have no --reflog, so REG-22's fact (2) and the stop rule's check are not "these three commands" (CG8).
>
> **The freeze (stop entry item 5, which is BK-S4).**
> - The text keeps the freeze, both facts, the validity cut and the not-computed rules.
> - `git log --all --full-history ffc76b3..HEAD` over the 27 files prints nothing, at 128fd88 and again at 5f782d6. `git status` on them prints nothing.
> - closure.py at HEAD equals closure_c2_20261113T173125Z.txt.
> - But see CG2: the facts now only add label words, which does not close BK-S4's own trace.
